# Changelog — pdfmd.py

Newest first. Versions follow semver loosely: a **major** bump changes
behavior in a way that could surprise an existing user (a default flips, a
flag's meaning changes). One **minor** bump (`3.N.0`) opens a feature line,
however large it is; every change after it in that line is a **patch**
(`3.N.x`), whatever it adds, so the version count stays small.

The version string lives in one place, the `PDFMD_VERSION` line of `pdfmd.py`
(a little below its module docstring; `pyproject.toml` and the publish workflow
read it from there):

```python
PDFMD_VERSION = "2.0.0"
```

`pdfmd --version` prints it. Bump it there and add an entry here in the
same commit as the change.

---

## v3.33.183 — 2026-11-12

Pre-edit state: commit `6ab9c87`. Review finding G4.4: `/api/render` of `pdfmd --serve` checked the document's own path but ran
pdfmd's filters on whatever the TEXT names, so `::: {.csv file="../private.txt"}` (or an absolute path, or a link in the project
pointing out of it) had `csv_table.lua` open a file outside the project and put it in the page, against the documented boundary.
Pandoc runs the `init.lua` of its data folder before every Lua filter, so each live render now gets a data folder of its own
(`lib/pdfmd_serve/contain.py`) whose `init.lua` wraps the Lua functions that open a file by name (`io.open`, `io.lines`, `io.input`,
`io.output`, `dofile`, `loadfile`, `os.remove`, `os.rename`, `pandoc.mediabag.fetch`). A path is let through when it lies in the
folder of one of the render's filters, in pdfmd's cache (named by the server: `Core(places=...)`, the pictures of diagrams, LaTeX
pieces and structures) or in the render's own temporary folder (TMPDIR points there); otherwise only when its real path, resolved by
the operating system through a small Python check (symlinks and `..` after a link included), is inside the project and not in `.git`.
A refused file fails as a missing one does, with one warning the page shows. Not covered, and said so in the README: a program a
filter starts (a LaTeX picture's `\input`, a diagram tool's include) reads what it is told. What it costs: a file outside the project
that a setting names (a shared LaTeX preamble) is not read by the live view's filters either, a file of the project costs one short
Python start the first time a filter opens it, and the live view no longer uses Pandoc's user data folder (no templates are used there;
an `init.lua` of the user's own is not run). Regression: `tests/test_serve.py` renders `../secret.csv`, its absolute path,
`sub/../../secret.csv`, a file link, a folder link and `..` after a link that stays inside (the links where symlinks exist): none
reaches the page and each warns; `../inside.csv` from `sub/` and an absolute path inside still are tables. Checked failing without the
guard (the secret in the table) and passing with it; `scripts/pdfmd --api POST /api/render` in a scratch project refuses a secret beside
it while a CSV of the project and a Graphviz diagram (through the cache) still render. pdfmd.py stays at 17,136 lines.

## v3.33.182 — 2026-11-12

Pre-edit state: commit `18e7d8c`. Review finding G4.2: `GET /api/file` of `pdfmd --serve` (and `--api`) read a file's bytes
first and took the mtime it answers with afterwards. A file replaced between the two came back as the old text with the new
file's mtime, and a save sending that mtime back was accepted: the replacement, which nobody had seen, was overwritten. This
needs no coarse timestamps, only a write landing during the read. The mtime is now taken before the bytes are read, so it can be
older than the text but never newer: a change during the read makes the next save a 409 conflict (the page then says the file
changed on disk) instead of an overwrite. No retry loop and no new setting; the API's shape and meaning are unchanged.
Regression: `tests/test_serve.py` replaces the file, with a clearly newer mtime, right after its bytes are read, and checks that
the save is refused and the replacement kept; checked failing before (200) and passing after (409). A read and a save through
`scripts/pdfmd --api` still round-trip. pdfmd.py stays at 17,136 lines.

## v3.33.181c — 2026-11-12

Pre-edit state: commit `5b329f4`. `gui/` only, no shipped pdfmd code, so no `PDFMD_VERSION` bump. **Colophon 0.3.4: the
popup's preamble and metadata panes no longer overwrite a file changed elsewhere.** Review finding G3.1: the pane writes its
file at every key press, the whole text at once, and did so without looking at the disk: with the pane open, a change made to
`preamble.tex` (or `pdfmd-metadata.yaml`) in another editor was replaced by the pane's older text at the next key press. The
pane now keeps the bytes it read (or last wrote) and `PopController.savePane` compares them with the disk before writing; when
the file changed meanwhile, an alert offers Keep Mine (the file is replaced) or Load the File on Disk (the typing is dropped and
the pane shows the file). A file that is gone is written again, and a failed write now says so in the status line instead of
being ignored. Regression: `--smoke-pop` (headless, on its scratch folder) changes the scratch preamble behind the pane and checks
Load, a plain edit afterwards with no question, and Keep Mine; checked failing with the old unconditional write and passing now.

## v3.33.181b — 2026-11-12

Pre-edit state: commit `d1731fc`. `gui/` only, no shipped pdfmd code, so no `PDFMD_VERSION` bump. **Colophon 0.3.3: a link in
the studio's live view no longer replaces the page.** Review finding G4.3: a preview link such as `[notes](notes.md)` resolves
against the page's address (`http://127.0.0.1:PORT/notes.md`), and the navigation policy let every address of host `127.0.0.1`
load in the window: the whole studio page, unsaved edits included, was replaced, usually by a 404. The policy now treats only
same-page anchors and the frames inside the page as navigation; a link to the studio's own server opens the project file it names
in a tab of the page (`WebStudioController.projectFile`: tried beside the current file first, as a file of `parts/` resolves
against the folder's top, then from the top; never a folder or a path outside the project), any other link that is not to the web
does nothing (a beep), and a script or form leaving the page asks first while something is unsaved. A web link still opens in the
browser, now also one to another local port. Regression: `--smoke-web` gains the link checks (a project file opens in a tab and
the page keeps its edits, a missing file and a script leave the page alone, the name lookups); run headless on a window that was
never shown, they failed with the old policy (the page went to `/report.md`) and pass now; `--smoke-web` itself puts a window on
screen and is for the reviewer to run.

## v3.33.181a — 2026-11-12

Pre-edit state: commit `fb02b26`. `gui/` only, no shipped pdfmd code, so no `PDFMD_VERSION` bump. **Colophon 0.3.2: the
hand-over to the studio keeps what was typed meanwhile.** Review finding G2.2: switching an unsaved new editor window to the
studio (control-command-S) took its text at once, and when the studio, still starting `pdfmd --serve`, had made a tab of it,
the editor window's change count was cleared and the window closed unconditionally; anything typed in it during the wait was
lost. `AppDelegate.finishHandover` now closes the window only when it still holds the very text that was handed over; when it
does not, the window stays open and edited, and an alert says that the studio's new tab has the text as it was at the switch.
A window closed meanwhile is left alone. Regression: `--smoke-untitled` (headless) hands over an unchanged window (closed) and
one typed in afterwards (kept, edited, with the new text); checked failing with the old unconditional close and passing now.

## v3.33.181 — 2026-11-12

Pre-edit state: commit `b2ad299`. **Colophon 0.3.1.** Review findings G2.1 and G4.1 (one fix): quitting Colophon (⌘Q, a logout)
discarded the studio window's unsaved edits without a word. The studio is a window controller, not an `NSDocument`, so the
document controller's review before quitting never saw it; its own question lived in `windowShouldClose`, which quitting
bypasses, and the only quit handler stopped the servers. The app delegate now answers `applicationShouldTerminate`: with a
studio window open it waits (`terminateLater`) while each studio asks its page whether anything is unsaved (the page itself,
since the state it last posted can be a key press late) and, if so, asks Save, Don't Save or Cancel. Save writes every tab
with changes; a refused save (the file changed on disk) or Cancel keeps the app running. The page gains `window.appDirty()`
and `window.appSaveAll()` for this (`lib/pdfmd_web/js/app.js`, hence the version); a page served by an older pdfmd has
neither, and the window then goes by the state it was told and refuses the quit on Save. Regression: `tests/test_web.py`
drives `appSaveAll` over changed, unchanged, refused and picture tabs (checked failing before, passing after); `--smoke-web`
gains the quit checks (Cancel, Don't Save, the page asked over a stale state, Save writing a real file through
`pdfmd --serve`), to be run by hand as it puts a window on screen. pdfmd.py stays at 17,136 lines.

## v3.33.180 — 2026-11-12

Pre-edit state: commit `2cf014b`. DECISION 50: `.odt` used Pandoc's OpenDocument writer by default, dropping raw Word blocks
such as a cover or form and the Word route's extras. The deferred pdfmd_bridge.odt helper now runs the complete Word build
and the existing LibreOffice converter; auto falls back to Pandoc when LibreOffice is missing or conversion fails, with
one warning naming the losses and asking for LibreOffice. `odt.engine: auto | soffice | pandoc` has a setup row, unset words,
folder support, inventory coverage and documentation; command-line `-e soffice` / `-e pandoc` wins. An OpenDocument reference
(`.odt`/`.ott`), named or discovered, selects Pandoc in auto with a note. Regression: route mocks and isolated scripts/pdfmd
builds check raw OOXML in the Word intermediate, conversion failure, missing LibreOffice, explicit choices, CLI precedence
and reference selection; checked failing before and passing after. The real LibreOffice conversion skips when missing or
unable to start, including the Codex sandbox; it must be run outside that sandbox. pdfmd.py grows from 17,133 to 17,136 lines
for the deferred dispatch and the exception to the ignored-engine warning; all new route logic lives in the package.

## v3.33.179a — 2026-11-12

Pre-edit state: commit `9459f2b`. A test only, from the third CI run of the 3.33.17x fixes (`native`, Windows, Python 3.9,
3.10 and 3.13: one failure each, the only one left there). `test_batch_paths.Checkout.test_same_pdf_destination_prefers_markdown`
builds a document named in Cyrillic and looks for its name in pdfmd's NOTE line. The test reads the child's output as UTF-8,
but on Windows outside Python's UTF-8 mode a pipe is in the code page (cp1252 on the runner), where pdfmd since v3.33.175
prints `?` for a character the page cannot show instead of ending the run: the run worked, and the line said
`NOTE  skipped (same output as ???????? ? ????????.md)`. Python 3.15, in UTF-8 mode by default, passed. The class's child
processes now get `PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8`, so they write what the test reads; the assertion is unchanged. A user's console
is unaffected (Python writes to a Windows console in Unicode).

## v3.33.179 — 2026-11-12

Pre-edit state: commit `f8d120d`. DECISION 53 item 4: named Lua filters and preambles were read only from the document, silently ignoring metadata and setup layers. The shared pdfmd_assemble.named resolver now follows document > metadata files > folder layers > global setup, retaining each naming file as the base for relative paths. As with other list-valued options, the nearest ordinary list replaces lower lists; `key+:` (and `key+=:`) explicitly appends from lower to higher layers. Flat and grouped spellings still add within one layer. Effective missing files remain hard errors, with the existing assembled Lua-reference exception; Lua trust checks include filters run during assembly. Global/folder setup gains both list rows and inventory coverage. Batch, report, kit, CSS and kept-source callers pass their actual metadata files; embedded append names are cleared once their files are included. Regression: metadata-relative, folder, global, document, grouped, replacement, append, missing-file and trust checks; the initial layer tests failed before and pass after, including real scripts/pdfmd HTML/LaTeX builds and an assembly. pdfmd.py shrinks from 17,211 to 17,133 lines.

## v3.33.175 — 2026-11-12

Pre-edit state: commit `46f159c`. v3.33.170's `tolerant_streams()` did not help on Windows itself: the second CI run still ended `pdfmd "Документ с пробелом.md" …` with a `UnicodeEncodeError` traceback on Python 3.9, 3.10 and 3.13 (the `native (windows-latest, …)` jobs, five tests of `test_batch_paths.Checkout`; 3.15 passes because its output is UTF-8). The cause: the function replaced only the `strict` error handler, but Python on Windows gives a piped standard output `surrogateescape`, which in a code page raises for a missing character exactly as `strict` does; v3.33.170's tests simulated the pipe with a strict stream. `lib/pdfmd_view`'s new `raises_for_missing()` names both cases: `strict` always, `surrogateescape` unless the encoding is a UTF (there it never raises for a real character and passes undecodable file-name bytes through, so it is kept). Such a stream gets `replace`, as before. Test: `test_batch_paths.CodePageStreams.test_the_handler_windows_gives_a_pipe_is_replaced_in_a_code_page_only` (the handler stayed `surrogateescape` before; a UTF-8 stream keeps it). `pdfmd.py` is unchanged (17,217 lines).

Pre-edit state: commit `bab6795`. `test_engine_filters.Filter.test_the_space_between_paragraphs` collected every line of a standalone Typst document that holds `spacing` and a `#`, and expected only pdfmd's `#set par(leading: ..., spacing: ...)`. Pandoc 3.1.3 defines an `endnote` function in every standalone Typst document, with a `#stack(dir: ltr, spacing: 3pt, super[#num], contents)` line, so the list had two entries and the test failed in the linux-pandoc job for 3.1.3; pdfmd's own rule was there, unchanged. Pre-edit state: commit `de6dc1a`. `test_newline.Build.test_outside_a_vault_a_newline_is_a_space_and_every_writer_takes_the_break` failed on the CI job `linux-pandoc (Pandoc 3.1.3)`, where it had never run: it asked for the Typst text `line one \ line two`, and Pandoc 3.1.3's Typst writer puts a new line after the backslash where a newer one puts a space. ## v3.33.174 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `5cb30bc`. The warning for a `$...$` that Pandoc reads as text because a digit follows the closing dollar (`$\geq$3`) named lines that were read as math, on Pandoc 3.1.3 with the gfm reader. That reader has no digit rule there: `$\geq$3` is math followed by `3`, and there is nothing to warn about. But a copy with the dollars escaped (`\$\geq\$3`) is the plain text `$\geq$3` in what any reader gives, `nonmath_dollars()` took it for a failed span, and then looked the text up in the source, where only the unescaped copies match: they got the warning. The trigger was the CI job `linux-pandoc (Pandoc 3.1.3)`, on `test_nonmath_dollars.FindingThem.test_the_gfm_reader_keeps_the_whole_thing_as_one_word` (lines 1 and 11 named instead of 1, 5 and 11: both are math on that Pandoc, and line 5, which has no escaped twin, was rightly silent). Now the copies are counted: when the copies of the text with a dollar escaped in the source account for every one the reader gave, the unescaped ones were read as math and nothing is said. On a newer Pandoc, where the reader keeps the unescaped span as text, the count is higher and the warning stands as before. The fix is in `nonmath_dollars()` where it sits, so `pdfmd.py` is 7 lines longer (17208 to 17215). Tests: the test above now asks Pandoc how its gfm reader takes `$\geq$3` and expects no line where it is math and 1, 5, 11 where it is text (it failed on 3.1.3, passes on 3.1.3 and 3.13); `test_an_escaped_copy_is_not_taken_for_the_unescaped_one` is new and gives the reader's answer itself, so it runs the same on any Pandoc.

## v3.33.173 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `8d0fc85`. `[flavours]` On Pandoc 3.1.3 a file without front matter got no figures: `![The caption](pic.png)` alone in its paragraph, and a picture embed with a caption (`![[pic.png|Caption|100]]`), stayed an inline image whose caption was only its alt text, in every writer. The pdfmd and obsidian flavours read such a file as `gfm+smart+implicit_figures`; the gfm reader of 3.1.3 lists the extension and accepts it, and does nothing with it (a newer one makes the figure; Pandoc's own Markdown reader always did, so a file with front matter was right). The trigger was the CI job `linux-pandoc (Pandoc 3.1.3)`: `test_obsidian.CommandLine.test_the_pdfmd_flavour_reads_typography_figures_bare_links_and_emoji_on_both_readers` (the gfm subtest) and `test_embeds.Build.test_outside_a_vault_it_is_pdfmds_own_embed_and_flavour_pandoc_leaves_it_text`, neither of which had run there. The new `lib/pdfmd_lua/figures.lua` does what the reader would have done, in the same shape: a paragraph that holds one image with a caption and nothing else becomes a Figure, the image's identifier goes to the figure. It reads the reader's own extensions (`PANDOC_READER_OPTIONS`) and acts only when figures were asked for, so `--from gfm` and `flavour: gfm` still get none, and where the reader made the figures no such paragraph is left and it changes nothing: it is told by what the reader left, not by a version number. `figure_filter_args()` (`lib/pdfmd_obsidian/vault.py`) adds it, before the markup filter, for a Markdown document with `![` in it whose flavour asks the gfm reader for figures. `pdfmd.py` is one line longer (17207 to 17208: the name's `deferred()` line; the call is on the embed filter's line). Tests: the gfm subtest failed on 3.1.3 and passes on 3.1.3 and 3.13; `test_a_figure_is_made_where_the_gfm_reader_does_not_make_it` is new (one figure, the caption's emphasis kept, no figure for a picture inside a sentence, for one with no caption, or with the extension off).

## v3.33.172 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `2a5ef9b`. `[serve]` The live view of `pdfmd --serve` on Pandoc 3.1.3 showed none of pdfmd's own syntax and kept a span around every word. Pandoc's `sourcepos` wraps each word in a span and each plain block in a div; a newer Pandoc marks those with `wrapper="1"`, and both `lib/pdfmd_lua/sourcepos.lua` (which puts the document back as the reader gives it, before pdfmd's filters) and `strip_wrappers()` of `lib/pdfmd_serve/core.py` knew a wrapper only by that mark. Pandoc 3.1.3 writes the same wrappers without it, so calc never saw its `{=}` beside the code, a callout was a block quote, and the HTML was `<span data-pos=...>` word by word. The trigger was the CI job `linux-pandoc (Pandoc 3.1.3)`, which had never run these tests: `test_serve.Render.test_render_gives_blocks_with_positions_and_no_word_wrappers`, `test_render_of_what_is_not_written_yet` and `test_the_live_view_shows_pdfmds_syntax_as_a_build_does`. Now a wrapper is also the span or div with no identifier, no class and nothing but positions as attributes (the wrapper of a list item has two there), and the Python side takes out the span whose only attribute is `data-pos`; a span the author wrote with a class of its own stays on both. Pandoc 3.1.3 also warns about its own second position on every list item ("Ignoring duplicate attribute data-pos"): that line is dropped from the render's warnings beside the `--mathml` one (`PANDOC_NOISE`). On 3.1.3 a plain block keeps its position on a div around it, where a newer Pandoc writes it on the block; the page reads either. Tests: the three above failed on 3.1.3 and pass on 3.1.3 and 3.13; `test_the_word_wrappers_of_an_older_pandoc_go_too` is new and needs no Pandoc.

## v3.33.171 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `914b558`. **Two writers of one cache entry survive Windows refusing the rename.** A converted SVG, a fetched remote image and an emoji picture are written whole to a `.part` file beside the cache entry and renamed over it, so two builds never share a half-written file; on Windows the rename itself is refused with `PermissionError: [WinError 5] Access is denied` while another writer is renaming onto the same target or a reader holds it, and the build that lost stopped with a traceback. Shown by the first CI run of the 3.33 line: `test_images.ConcurrentCaching.test_svg_writers_do_not_share_a_partial_file` (`native`, Windows, Python 3.9; `write_cached()` in `lib/pdfmd_images/cache.py`) and `test_unicode.ColourEmoji.test_parallel_picture_writers_use_distinct_temporary_files` (the same job and `windows-latex`; `write_pictures()` in `lib/pdfmd_unicode/colorfont.py`, which had a second copy of the same code). `atomic_file()` in `pdfmd.py` does not handle this either and is for files that are rewritten in place, so there is now one writer for cache entries, `pdfmd_cache.write_cached()`; `pdfmd_images.cache.write_cached` is that function and `write_pictures()` calls it. A cache entry is named by its content, so both writers carry the same bytes: when the rename is refused and the target already holds exactly these bytes the writer is done; otherwise it tries again, `REPLACE_TRIES` = 20 times with `REPLACE_PAUSE` = 0.05 s between (one second at most), and a refusal that lasts is still raised; the `.part` file is removed in every case. The two numbers are constants in `lib/pdfmd_cache`, not settings (a file-system fact with no sensible knob; the author is told). `pdfmd.py` is unchanged. Tests: `test_images.RefusedReplace`, four, with `Path.replace` patched to raise the Windows error on any system: the other writer's identical file is success after one try; a refusal with no file yet is tried again and the file is written; a lasting refusal over a file with other bytes raises after `REPLACE_TRIES` tries and leaves no `.part`; the emoji pictures use the same writer. The first three failed before (the error was raised at the first refusal). The two CI tests are unchanged and must pass on the Windows runners.

## v3.33.170b — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `1bc63e8`. **The git-URL test of the kit installer names its local repository by a real file URL.** `test_kit_install.Git.test_a_git_url_and_a_ref` built the URL as `f"file://{repo}"`, which is `file:///tmp/...` on macOS and Linux but `file://C:\Users\...\repo` on Windows: no URL at all (the drive becomes the host). `git fetch` happened to accept it, so the first half of the test (`@v1`) passed, and `git clone` did not: `InstallError: git clone failed: and the repository exists.` in every Windows job of the first CI run of the 3.33 line. The parser is not at fault: `parse_source()` splits `file:///C:/Users/x/repo@v1` into the URL and the ref (the `@` after the path, the drive colon and a `~` of a short name do not disturb it), and what it hands to git is what the user wrote. The test now writes `"file:///" + repo.as_posix().lstrip("/")`, the form the error message of a folder with `@ref` already recommends (`file:///path`), and `Parse.test_forms` has three `file:///` sources (a Windows drive with a space and a ref, a short name with a ref and a kit's name, a POSIX path) so the split is checked on every system; they pass with the code as it is.

## v3.33.170 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `180d356`. **No message can end a run with `UnicodeEncodeError`.** On Windows before Python 3.15 a pipe, a redirected output or a console that is not UTF-8 is in the ANSI code page (cp1252 on the runners), and Python's standard output is strict about it: the first line that named a file with letters outside that page (`NATIVE Документ с пробелом.md via inkmd`, printed by `convert_native()` through the build's `_WarningTee` and `_RecordTee` wrappers, which pass the text on to the real stream) raised `UnicodeEncodeError` in `encodings/cp1252.py` and the build died with a traceback. v3.25.19 had repaired only `--help` (its own `_write()` prints `?` for such a character). Shown by the first CI run of the 3.33 line: five tests of `test_batch_paths.Checkout` (the ones that build the Cyrillic-named file) failed in the `native` Windows jobs with Python 3.9, 3.10 and 3.13, and not with 3.15, whose default is UTF-8. `pdfmd_view.tolerant_streams()` (new; `lib/pdfmd_view` is the terminal-output package that every run loads) now runs first in `main()` and in `restore_worker_state()` (a `-j` worker is a fresh process on Windows): a standard stream whose error handler is `strict` is reconfigured to `replace`, the same `?` as `--help`; the encoding stays as it is, a handler somebody chose (`PYTHONIOENCODING=utf-8:surrogateescape`, standard error's `backslashreplace`) stays, and a stream with no `reconfigure` (a `StringIO`) is left alone. Because it is the stream that changes, every `print` of pdfmd and of its packages is covered, through the wrappers too. `pdfmd.py` grows by two lines (17207 to 17209): the two calls, which must sit where a process starts. Tests: `test_batch_paths.CodePageStreams`, three: a cp1252 stream that raised prints `NATIVE ????????.md via inkmd — é` through `_WarningTee` after the call; a chosen handler, a `StringIO` and a closed stream are left alone; and the checkout's `pdfmd` run with `PYTHONIOENCODING=cp1252` on the Cyrillic-named file, alone and with `-b -j 2`, ends with status 0 and the `NATIVE` line (both subtests failed before with the traceback, on every system).

Pre-edit state: commit `c26fc88`. Uncached natbib and biblatex builds ran the markup filter without its LaTeX header, leaving callouts and highlighted text undefined at compilation. ## v3.33.151 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `1c1b737`. A margin-only Office override made has_page true and replaced a reference document’s dimensions and orientation with the Letter defaults. ## v3.33.150 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `813f3dd`. Office inputs resolved hybrid attachments from user configuration alone, excluding folder settings that enabled the feature or overrode a user-wide enable. No new setting or behavioural threshold.

## v3.33.149 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `15dd600`. Batch builds omitted the command-line cache override when calling the converter, allowing document settings to defeat both --cache and --no-cache in sequential and parallel runs. Both calls now pass cache_cli=args.cache. Checkout regressions failed before the fix in all four switch/worker combinations and pass afterwards, checking persistent cache manifests as well as PDFs; batch-path, cache-location and repository guard tests run. pdfmd.py remains 17,204 lines. ## v3.33.148 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `3c702e5`. Parts builds scanned only the scaffold for hand-typed table captions and line breaks, so syntax present only in a part lost its filters. Both detectors now scan the complete input list and retain its first file, the scaffold, as their settings source. Checkout regressions failed before the fix for both filters and pass afterwards, including disabled scaffold settings; caption, line-break, parts and repository guard tests run. pdfmd.py remains 17,204 lines. No new setting or behavioural threshold.

## v3.33.147b — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `3814f05`. LibreOffice aborts inside the Codex sandbox even in headless mode, raising crash dialogues during tests. The test isolation helper now writes soffice-timeout: 0 into its temporary user configuration when CODEX_SANDBOX is set; tests that explicitly require LibreOffice skip with the reason. Outside the sandbox the configuration is unchanged. The inherited-configuration regression failed before the fix and passes afterwards; Office modules and the repository guards run, with read-only crash-report name counts checked before and afterwards. ## v3.33.147 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `420d3fb`. Front matter closed with ... was recognised by Pandoc but missed by font and margin handling, allowing defaults to override document settings and leaving scalar Typst margins invalid. Font detection, geometry detection, LaTeX margin translation and Typst margin rewriting now share the front-matter fence matcher, which captures the YAML block and preserves either terminator. Regressions failed before the fix and pass afterwards, including checkout LaTeX and Typst output, body preservation and operation without PyYAML; metadata-append, kit-carry, Unicode, paper, math-font and repository guard tests run. pdfmd.py remains 17,204 lines. No new setting or behavioural threshold.

## v3.33.146 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `3a8f506`. Font lookup inspected metadata files in input order rather than winning order; a managed font found in the weaker file could then be injected with -V over the stronger file. Lookup now follows metadata_files_by_priority, retaining document and command-line priority and the first-file precedence setting. Lookup and checkout regressions with a scratch managed font failed before the fix and pass afterwards; Unicode and repository guard tests run. pdfmd.py remains 17,204 lines. No new setting or behavioural threshold.

## v3.33.145 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `cfa9016`. Metadata files closed with a valid --- fence were parsed as multiple YAML documents, silently losing pdfmd settings while Pandoc still read its metadata. The metadata reader now uses the shared front-matter parser for supported fences and retains bare YAML parsing. Engine-setting and checkout code-numbering regressions failed before the fix and pass afterwards, covering both fence terminators and bare files; configuration, engine-chain and repository guard tests run. pdfmd.py remains 17,204 lines. No new setting or behavioural threshold.

## v3.33.144 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `8849549`. Global code settings skipped linked metadata files and were emitted as overrides, so a metadata-file line-numbers: false could still produce numbered blocks. Every code-filter route now receives metadata files and resolves each key through the normal option sources below the command line. Checkout regressions failed before the fix and pass afterwards for metadata disabling global numbering, document enabling it with a metadata-file step, and command-line overrides; code-block and repository guard tests run. pdfmd.py shrinks from 17,206 to 17,204 lines. No new setting or behavioural threshold.

## v3.33.143 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `5a97ee8`. Appending a document metadata value could overwrite an explicit command-line value because the append filter replaced Pandoc’s resolved metadata. Append replacements now exclude keys explicitly supplied with command-line metadata, preserving unrelated appends. Checkout regressions for separate and attached -M forms, with equals and colon separators, failed before the fix and pass afterwards; metadata-append and repository guard tests run. Option scanning lives in the argument package; pdfmd.py grows from 17,204 to 17,206 lines to remove those keys from its existing merge. No new setting or behavioural threshold.

## v3.33.142 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `9aede11`. Disabled aliases such as files, blanket no-auto and explicit-only survived precedence resolution and were expanded again, defeating a stronger per-kind on setting. Alias expansion now produces concrete kinds before resolving layers, including blanket disabling. Regressions failed before the fix and pass afterwards, including a checkout HTML build that restores document-requested Lua discovery; automatic-kind, setup, Unicode, serve and repository guard tests run. pdfmd.py remains 17,204 lines; no new setting or behavioural threshold.

## v3.33.141 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `1016a0c`. Reference-number PDF builds inherited a non-LaTeX engine and could recursively launch pdfmd when Office LaTeX conversion was enabled. The helper now selects installed LaTeX engines, excludes ConTeXt (which has no LaTeX counters), and disables nested Office conversion; without a suitable engine it retains counted numbers. Regressions failed before the fix and pass afterwards; a checkout HTML build with a Typst document setting, Office tests and the repository guards are checked. The helper lives in the Office package; pdfmd.py shrinks from 17,211 to 17,204 lines. No new setting or behavioural threshold.

## v3.33.140 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `81f311a`. Inputs such as `a.md` and an earlier `a.html` could both build to `a.pdf`, silently
replacing the first result. Inputs with the same resolved planned destination now build once, preferring Markdown, other
text markup, HTML, then office and e-book formats, with name order breaking ties; the NOTE names the skipped inputs and
chosen source. Collision skips now have their own note naming the winning input, separate from non-input and built-output notes;
the checkout wording regressions failed before that correction and pass afterwards (pre-edit state: commit `16932ff`). Checkout regressions failed before the fix and pass afterwards for Markdown and HTML, HTML and DOCX,
a Cyrillic spaced name, and a shared output folder.

A repeated multi-path build could treat its earlier HTML or other readable output as a source, then fail on a
self-overwrite. Selection now skips and names outputs belonging to another selected input, using the batch target and
output-extension rules, while retaining unrelated inputs and the existing rewrite behaviour. Checkout-launcher
regressions failed before the fix and pass afterwards, including output folders, compound extensions and Cyrillic names.
Pre-fix state: commit `db5f3d9`.

Pre-edit state: commit `9a194d3`. **Build several input paths separately.** The author's explicit-file batch
failed because `-b` required one folder; plain multiple paths also failed. Batch mode now accepts mixed files and
folders, and multiple paths without `-r` use the same pipeline. Folder discovery retains its Markdown-only rules;
explicit Pandoc inputs are deduplicated by resolved path. EPUBs use the existing scratch Markdown reader before
text-based metadata inspection, retaining their resources, output folders and display names in workers too.
PDFs and other non-inputs are skipped in one NOTE, with
an output-naming hint for a PDF beside an input in the two-path case; an empty selection fails. Single-file mode,
report merging and compatibility output arguments retain their meanings. Output filenames and existing single-document
restrictions are refused for batches; output folders and workers apply across the selection.

Selection and validation live in `lib/pdfmd_batch`; `pdfmd.py` grows by one dispatch line (17,211 to 17,212 lines) to
route batches before the special single-file readers. Help, the README, recipes and agent guide describe the inputs.
Regression tests failed before the fix and pass afterwards, including checkout-launcher builds with synthetic names
containing spaces, Cyrillic and brackets, earlier PDF outputs, mixed folders, duplicate paths, attachments, parallel
workers, other Pandoc formats, single-file PDF routing and compatibility commands. Area tests and the required split,
packaging, documentation, setup and isolation checks run. No new setting or behavioural threshold is introduced.

## v3.33.139 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `85e665f`. **Repair the full-screen Windows PATH action.** Selecting the action passed
the screen input object as a prompt, causing a TypeError and losing unsaved edits. The menu now receives the terminal
input function; a real menu regression and PATH, setup and repository guard tests run.

## v3.33.138 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `5edb820`. **Validate table counts in setup.** Both editors rejected zero and accepted
`all` for table keep and caption word counts, although the build readers require non-negative integers. The rows now
validate accordingly; editor regressions and setup and repository guard tests run.

## v3.33.137 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `b0ea9d2`. **Keep a report’s sole later title.** When only a later file supplied a title,
report assembly stripped it with that file’s front matter. The title and subtitle now move to the first file; a
checkout report regression and report and repository guard tests run.

## v3.33.136 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `4ab9c62`. **Use the fresh Biber control file.** A stale control file beside a direct TeX
source could override the fresh scratch copy, producing outdated citations. Biber now receives the absolute scratch
control path while retaining bibliography lookup; a checkout regression and TeX and repository guard tests run.

## v3.33.135 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `6f6dfd2`. **Keep native Calibre image paths usable.** Moving normalised Markdown to
scratch made relative images resolve there instead of beside the source. Image references now point back to the
source base; a checkout regression with a stand-in Calibre and the native and repository guard tests run.

## v3.33.134 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `b09c66e`. **Protect TeX files with spaces from fallback.** File-and-line diagnostics
with spaces or quoted names were classified as engine failures, allowing a lossy retry to replace a PDF. The
classifier now recognises these filenames; classifier and checkout build regressions and repository guard tests run.

## v3.33.133 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `e8483a0`. **Handle decomposed accents in ASCII builds.** Combining accents were
reported as missing, so equivalent decomposed text failed where composed text passed. Normalise text and remove
remaining combining accents; transliteration and checkout ASCII-build regressions and repository guard tests run.

## v3.33.132 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `4c6ed44`. **Keep readable source names unambiguous.** A file ending in ` (base64)`
was mistaken for an encoded binary section and could crash restoration. New readable trailers encode names and
encodings separately; old trailers remain readable. Round-trip and checkout bundle-and-restore regressions and
the flat-source and repository guard tests run.

## v3.33.131 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `6935645`. **Retrieve history across renames.** Earlier commits were listed by Git's
followed history but read using the current name, so diff and restore failed. Retrieval now follows rename records
back to the selected commit; a checkout history-diff regression and the history and repository guard tests run.

## v3.33.130 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `7f125a2`. **Read Unicode names from Git history.** Git quoted non-ASCII file names,
so history could list commits but could not retrieve their contents. NUL-delimited `ls-files` output now retains
the path verbatim; a checkout history-diff regression and the history and repository guard tests run.

## v3.33.129 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `ed51822`. **Escape quoted template metadata.** Quotes and backslashes in template
values broke YAML front matter generated by `--init`. Double-quoted placeholder scalars now escape their values;
a checkout regression parses the generated title and the template and repository guard tests run.

## v3.33.128 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `4fbc5fa`. **Honour image mode for raw equation blocks.** Raw LaTeX equation environments
and bracketed displays became native maths even with `office: {latex: images}`. Both block handlers now guard
the native branch with the same image-mode check as the inline handler, allowing fragment rendering instead.
A checkout regression verifies two pictures rather than native maths in Word, two image references in Typst and
HTML, retained raw LaTeX, and unchanged native maths in auto mode; office and repository guard tests also run.

## v3.33.127 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `14f775f`. **Preserve class options when adding a cover.** With `cover: true` and a list
such as `[twoside, draft]`, the cover filter nested the existing list and LaTeX received `twosidedraft` as one option.
It now recognises Pandoc metadata lists with `pandoc.utils.type` and appends directly. A checkout regression checks

## v3.33.126 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `ad125e6`. **Convert nested raw HTML before inserting its wrapper.** With `--raw`, an image
or italic tag inside a bold HTML span disappeared from LaTeX and Typst because the outer conversion skipped its

rules before insertion. A checkout regression checks one retained image, nested italics and surrounding text in

## v3.33.125 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `b64a8b6`. **Read chemistry declarations from header metadata.** Custom units declared
in `header-includes` were ignored because the shared chemistry client rejected Pandoc's userdata nodes. It now

## v3.33.124 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `afe876a`. **[tables] Keep untagged cells when applying horizontal table defaults.** A plain pipe
table with `table-align: centre` crashed during LaTeX conversion because the alignment wrapper measured missing

## v3.33.123 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `e4addd7`. **Keep preserved section numbers in flat partial builds.** Exporting a later
numbered part to GFM or text restarted its headings at one, although selection had preserved their whole-document
numbers. The flat filter now uses an existing heading number before calculating one. A checkout regression checks

## v3.33.122 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `4f2de7e`. **Preserve rounded values with away rounding.** The unconditional relative
correction added whole units to large integers and altered precise decimals, and could promote values below a half.
Rounding now separates the integer and fractional parts and recognises decimal half ties in the original units,

## v3.33.121 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `ff873da`. **Keep remainder operators before signed divisors.** Inline calculations such as

signed divisors and a signed parenthesised operand in generated LaTeX, Typst and HTML.

## v3.33.120 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `33d4237`. **[tables] Retain CSV widths when expanding tables.** Short expanded pipe tables
lost chosen column widths because Pandoc ignored their separator proportions. Expansion now records widths in the

## v3.33.119 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `57a4089`. **[tables] Protect pipes inside code and maths from cell tags.** Splitting a table

## v3.33.118 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `fcefbd7`. **Use hyperref anchors to name office references.** Without cleveref, a figure's
auxiliary entry lost its type and `\autoref` called it a section. The parser now reads recognised anchor types,

## v3.33.117 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `e617756`. **Find reference-style images and balanced destinations.** Markdown images

SVG conversion. The scanner resolves reference labels and reads balanced destinations; a regression and a
checkout build cover both forms.

## v3.33.116 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `27b6d45`. **Avoid concurrent image cache collisions.** Parallel downloads and SVG
conversions shared partial filenames, so one writer could remove another's file before its rename. Both paths now
write unique temporary files and replace the target atomically; concurrent-writer regressions cover each path.

## v3.33.115 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `3f4441e`. **Keep office figure caches distinct.** Documents with different PDFs named
`plot.pdf` could reuse the first figure when its cached conversion was newer. The store now includes the resolved

## v3.33.114 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `3ecb803`. **Recognise keycap emoji for picture fallback.** A keycap whose digit was in the
main font was treated as a missing combining mark instead of an emoji. Complete keycap sequences now reach the

## v3.33.113 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `be4474c`. **Analyse nested and indented code for font fallback.** Indented blocks and
fences inside quotations were missed by the source scanner, leaving monofont gaps undetected. Font analysis now

## v3.33.112 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `49255a8`. **Keep script-specific fallback font switches.** When one fallback family drew
both Greek and Hebrew, grouping by family lost Hebrew direction and script settings. Choices now retain their

## v3.33.111 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `7cb78ca`. **Avoid concurrent emoji cache writes colliding.** Parallel builds caching the
same emoji shared a temporary file, so one rename could make the other fail. Each writer now atomically replaces
the cache entry from its own temporary file; a concurrent-writer regression checks both results and cleanup.

## v3.33.110 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `77d205d`. **Preserve complete abstracts when flattening.** An abstract containing several
paragraphs lost every block after the first in GFM and plain-text output. The title block now retains all abstract

cover both outputs and retained lists.

## v3.33.109 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `59c8ea0`. **[tables] Retain CSV fields beyond the header.** A data row wider than its header
silently lost its extra fields because row output used the header length. The filter now pads that header with empty
cells before applying the existing column limits; a full-pipeline regression covers longer and shorter rows, separator
alignment and capped columns.

## v3.33.108 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `41dc2f1`. **[smiles] Preserve all CRLF SD-file records.** Carriage returns prevented SD-file
delimiters from matching, so RDKit read only the first molecule. Molfile line endings are now normalised before
splitting, retaining blank title lines; regressions cover record counts and an isolated full build of a CRLF SD file.

## v3.33.107 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `94a542a`. **Match cached web previews to their source.** Rendering an edit and undoing to the
original text reused the edited HTML because the cache was keyed only by path and the original-text flag. Cached HTML
now carries the exact source text and is reused only for that text; a node regression renders edits and reversions
through scripts/pdfmd --api with isolated scratch folders.

## v3.33.106 — 2026-11-11

Pre-edit state: commit `436ab13`. **Track the text submitted by Save.** Typing while a save request was pending made the
newer, unwritten text appear saved. Save now captures its submitted snapshot and records only that snapshot as saved; a
delayed-response node regression checks the dirty indicator and the next save.

## v3.33.105 — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `d862f15`. **Keep web-editor Undo within its document.** Switching files recorded their
replacement text in one shared CodeMirror history, so Undo could put one file into another. Document switches now retain

installed esbuild and locked dependencies; node regressions exercise real CodeMirror history and tab switching. HTTP
checks were blocked by the sandbox’s socket-binding restriction.

## v3.33.104 — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `090adea`. **Preserve text after single-line LaTeX environments.** A raw environment opening and closing on one line left the native normaliser skipping the rest of the document. It now enters the skip state only when the closing tag is absent; regressions cover inkmd and Calibre normalisation and a full inkmd build.

## v3.33.103 — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `164cf4c`. **Ignore indented code in checks.** References and images in indented code
were reported as missing. The checker now masks code blocks while retaining paragraph and list continuations; a regression
covers spaces, tabs and both continuations.

## v3.33.102 — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `52ecb20`. **[kits] Accept slashes in repository refs.** A slash in `@REF` prevented its
recognition and could contaminate a Git URL. Parsing now distinguishes credentials from refs; regressions cover branch names,

## v3.33.101 — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `fc71eee`. **[tables] Protect fenced code after pipe tables.** Pipe-table scanning consumed
opening fences and allowed ASCII repair inside code examples. It now stops at fences, including indented fences; a regression
covers backticks and tildes.

## v3.33.100 — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `a0e5d27`. **[tables] Preserve blank spreadsheet cells with pandas.** Pandas represented blank
cells as NaN, causing conversion to fail. Missing cells are now normalised to empty cells; a regression checks both Python readers.

## v3.33.99 — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `c31f457`. **[tables] Detect auto delimiters during expansion.** Expanding a CSV block with
`delimiter="auto"` split on the letter a. Expansion now guesses the delimiter; a regression covers comma and semicolon data.

## v3.33.98 — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `a744ec3`. **Reserve generated title slugs before body headings.** Flattening inserted a title
after allocating heading anchors, so links to duplicate headings pointed to earlier headings. Slug allocation now
includes the generated title first. A regression checks two duplicate body headings with and without a title.

## v3.33.97 — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `a49f8f0`. **Close single-character highlights at their own delimiter.** A one-character
highlight missed its closer and consumed a later marked passage. The matching pattern now accepts one character.
A regression checks separate highlights in LaTeX, Typst and HTML.

## v3.33.96 — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `d0e9274`. **Include long-vowel marks in kana romanisation.** The Common-script mark split kana
runs, preventing Latin-name lookup of names such as スーパーマン. Marks adjacent to kana now join the kana run and are
handled by its existing romaniser. A regression checks the name and preserves standalone marks.

## v3.33.95 — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `ab3276d`. **Recognise drawable code emoji in the font check.** Emoji found only in code were
reported missing even when a colour emoji font could draw them. The check now considers body and code emoji together
for picture fallback. A regression checks the result with and without the font.

## v3.33.94 — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `01aad75`. **Use the effective body size for CSS headings.** A document fontsize overrode the
CSS body size, but relative heading sizes still used the rejected CSS value. Heading conversion now honours the document
size before the CSS fallback. A regression checks a 12pt document with an 11pt CSS body and a 2em heading.

## v3.33.93 — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `67064fa`. **Fix inkmd's equals-form stdout option.** `--out=-` parsed successfully but the
entry point searched for a separate `--out` token and raised a traceback. Output options are now normalised before
stdout handling. A regression runs the inkmd entry point and checks the PDF on stdout.

## v3.33.92b — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `809708d`. **Tests: `test_crop` no longer writes build records into the real cache.** Its second

## v3.33.92 — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `1db80de`. **Preserve disabled calculation and CSV features when editing their details.** Setup

checked failing before the fix and passing afterwards. Setup, CSV-switch and required checks run. `pdfmd.py` stays at
17,211 lines; no new thresholds.

## v3.33.91 — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `81d9a91`. **Keep a setup choice of no markup or page-break families disabled.** Both editors
removed an empty selection, letting the flavour's enabled defaults return. They now store an explicit empty list for these

## v3.33.90 — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `fce0501`. **Keep restored images distinct after an extension change.** Extracting both

## v3.33.73 — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `be4e402`. **Typst's line spacing is LaTeX's** (the author, 2026-11-10: "yes"; every Typst PDF's
look changes, which the author accepted). LaTeX puts lines `linestretch` x the class's `\baselineskip` apart (size10.clo,
size11.clo, size12.clo: 12, 13.6 and 14.5 TeX points), in any font. Pandoc's Typst template sets `leading: linestretch *
0.65em`, and Typst's line box runs from the font's cap height to the baseline, so its lines were leading + cap height apart:
23.48 pt at `linestretch: 2`, 12 pt, where LaTeX has 28.89, and 13.07 pt at `linestretch: 1`, 10 pt, where LaTeX has 11.95
(about 1.31em against 1.2). The longer the stretch, the further apart: a page held a quarter more lines in Typst.

- `pdfmd_lua/typst.lua` puts `#set text(top-edge: 0.7em, bottom-edge: "baseline")` and `#set par(leading: L, spacing: S)`
  at the top of the body of a standalone Typst document (`-e typst`, `-t typst -s`, `-r`, the office pre-pass route; a
  fragment, `-t typst` without `-s`, gets none). The box is the same for every font, and L is LaTeX's pitch less it, in em
  (so a heading or a footnote keeps the ratio): `linestretch` x `\baselineskip` / size x 72/72.27 (a TeX point is 1/72.27
  in, Typst's 1/72) - 0.7. The size is the `fontsize` (a `-V` variable first, then the metadata), else the template's 11pt;
  a size the standard classes do not have (14pt, or one not in pt) takes 1.2 x the size. In the body, not the
  header-includes: the template's own `set par(leading: ...)` sits inside `conf`, around the body, and wins over a header
  rule; a raw `#set par(leading: ...)` further down still wins over this one (tested). The title block keeps the template's
  leading. Constants (format facts, named in the filter): `BASELINESKIP` (10/11/12 pt), `TEX_POINT`, `TYPST_FONTSIZE` (11),
  `TYPST_SPACING_EM` (1.2, Typst's default `par.spacing`); a convention, `BASELINESKIP_RATIO` (1.2); a choice, `TOP_EDGE_EM`
  (0.7em, about a cap height: 0.66 to 0.72em in the usual fonts, so the room around a heading, a table row or a block moves
  by a fraction of a point; the pitch does not depend on it).
- The space between paragraphs keeps v3.33.58's meaning, now from the new leading: `indent: true` S = L (one line), and
  `paragraph-spacing X` S = L + X. With neither (`auto`, "each engine's own") Typst's own room is kept: its default spacing
  less its default leading, S = L + 0.55em, so a paragraph break is 0.55em more than a line at every `linestretch`, as it
  was at 1 (6.05 pt at 11 pt, unchanged). Typst's own 1.2em edge to edge had been less than a line from a `linestretch` of
  about 1.6: at 2 a paragraph break was 1.0 to 1.2 pt *closer* than the lines. The rule moved from the header-includes into
  the body block (an `--include-in-header` no longer drops it). v3.33.59's reference-list rule reads `par.leading` and
  `measure[X].height` where it runs, so it takes the new leading and box unchanged.
- Checked through pdfmd (`pdftotext -bbox-layout`, four 90-word paragraphs, LuaLaTeX against Typst; the line pitch, then
  the paragraph break less the pitch), STIX Two Text (pdfmd's default font) and Times New Roman alike to 0.01 pt:

  | size | linestretch | LuaLaTeX | Typst | Typst before | break-pitch LaTeX / Typst / before |
  |---|---|---|---|---|---|
  | 10 pt | 1 / 1.5 / 2 | 11.95 / 17.93 / 23.91 | 11.95 / 17.93 / 23.91 | 13.07 / 16.32 / 19.57 | 5.98 / 5.5 / 5.5, 2.25, -1.0 |
  | 11 pt | 1 / 1.5 / 2 | 13.55 / 20.32 / 27.10 | 13.55 / 20.32 / 27.10 | 14.38 / 17.95 / 21.53 | 6.77 / 6.05 / 6.05, 2.48, -1.1 |
  | 12 pt | 1 / 1.5 / 2 | 14.45 / 21.67 / 28.89 | 14.45 / 21.67 / 28.89 | 15.68 / 19.58 / 23.48 | 7.22 / 6.6 / 6.6, 2.7, -1.2 |

  (Typst before in Times New Roman: 13.12 to 23.55, 0.05 to 0.07 more, the cap heights' difference.) An APA 6 reference
  list (CSL entry-spacing 0, and a copy with 1), 12 pt Times New Roman, `linestretch` 1 and 2, plain, `indent: true` and
  `--paragraph-spacing 6pt`: inside an entry 14.45 / 28.89 in both engines; between entries the same with 0 and twice it

  each looked at side by side: the same lines at the same heights.

  file provider) could not be read (the provider timed out on every try), so it was built without

## v3.33.71 — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `c516381`. **`engine-fallback`: what a PDF engine's failure does** (the author's decision of 2026-11-10).
Any failure tried the next engine, and the degraded file (a Typst PDF after a LaTeX error in the document) replaced the good PDF
already there, with exit 0 (`--strict` made it exit 1, and still replaced it). New setting: `--engine-fallback MODE`,
`pdfmd-options: {engine-fallback: MODE}` (the document, its metadata files, a folder, the config), a `--setup` row (Output, *When a
PDF engine fails*).

- `on`: as before. `missing`: only an engine that cannot run here falls through, with `NOTE  doc.md: engine-fallback missing:
  lualatex counts as unusable here (...), not as an error in the document, so xelatex is tried`; an engine that ran and reported an
  error in the document stops the build. `off`: the first failure stops it. `auto`, **the default (a change of behaviour)**: a PDF
  that does not exist yet gets the whole chain, as `on`; for one that exists, the engine that made it is looked up, the chain
  starts with it (or the first engine of its family: LuaTeX, XeTeX, pdfTeX, the browsers, groff's two), the others following in
  their usual order, and the build behaves as `missing`. Nothing found: as `on`. A pinned engine (`-e X`, `-e A,B`,
  `pdf-engine:` anywhere, the config's default) is never reordered; `auto` with one is `missing` when the PDF exists, `on` when
  not. A bare `-e` pins nothing.
- Which engine made the PDF: pdfmd's own build record first (the newest `-ok` record whose `output:` is this file, `~` read as
  the home folder, and whose closing label shows no fallback: `(typst; lualatex failed)` is not mirrored, so a degraded build
  does not lock itself in, and when every record of the file fell back nothing is mirrored), else the PDF's Creator and Producer
  (Typst, LuaTeX, xdvipdfmx/XeTeX, pdfTeX, WeasyPrint, Prince, Edge's and Chrome's Skia, LibreOffice, Calibre, groff). The record
  already kept what is needed (the `result:` row's label), so its format is unchanged.
- What counts as the document's error (`failure_kind`): TeX, a `!` error line or a `-file-line-error` line (the direct `.tex`
  route), a missing `.sty` or `.cls` included; not the signatures of a broken or read-only installation (`TEX_UNUSABLE`, and the
  causes `TEX_CAUSES` names but a missing package). Typst: an `error:` with its place in the source. Pandoc's 47 (no such
  program) and every other failure count as the engine's.
- A stop: `WARN  doc.md: lualatex failed (! Undefined control sequence.); engine-fallback auto: an error in the document, so the
  build stops here and the existing doc.pdf is left as it was`, the place and cause lines as before, exit 1, and the closing line
  `FAIL  doc.md  (lualatex failed; engine-fallback auto stopped the build, doc.pdf kept; --engine-fallback on tries the next
  engine)`. A failed engine never writes the output (Pandoc writes it on success only; Calibre, the browsers and LibreOffice write
  into a scratch folder and copy on success), so the kept PDF is byte-identical. `--verbose`: `ENGINE  engine-fallback auto: doc.pdf
  was made by lualatex (build record 2026-11-10 13:40); starting with lualatex`.
- Where: `lib/pdfmd_chain` (new package: the mode, the lookup, the mirrored chain, the classification, `engine_failed`), called
  from the Markdown engine loop, the direct `.tex` loop (`compile_tex_direct`, which also serves the cache and natbib routes; a
  stopped `.tex` build no longer goes on through Pandoc, which drops the failing command and builds) and `-r`'s patch route (the
  default `-r` route is the Markdown loop). `pdfmd.py`: the plan call, the hooks, `ENGINE_CLI` and `ENGINE_FALLBACK_CLI` (set by
  `main`, carried to `-j` workers), the stopped text on `Built` for the closing line, `report_engine_failure(stopped=...)`.
  Unaffected: outputs other than PDF, `.typ` and `.html` inputs built by their own engine, the built-in renderers.
- Constants, all facts and no thresholds: `PANDOC_PROGRAM_NOT_FOUND = 47` (Pandoc's exit code), `TEX_UNUSABLE` (TeX's messages
  for a missing format, an unwritable file), `TEX_FILE_LINE_ERROR`, `TYPST_SOURCE_ERROR` (the engines' message layouts),
  `PRODUCERS` (what each engine writes in a PDF's Creator/Producer).
- Checked through pdfmd (scratch folders and config): `\undefinedcommandxyz` with no PDF there: lualatex, xelatex, pdflatex
  fail, Typst builds, as before; after a good LuaLaTeX build: stops, exit 1, sha256 the same; `--engine-fallback on`: Typst
  builds and replaces it; `missing` stops the same way; a fake `lualatex` on PATH that fails without a LaTeX error: auto and

longer stops after a preamble's soul.** pdfmd's `landscape` markup, on by default, loads pdflscape in its header file, which comes
after a kit's package; lscape defines `landscape` with `\def`, so it replaced a kit's own `\newenvironment{landscape}` without a
word. nulabreport's (a wider sheet, logo and footer upright: MediaBox 842 x 595, `/Rotate 0`) became pdflscape's turned portrait
page (595 x 842, `/Rotate 90`), and a grid table in it got the portrait width; in every report of the kit, with or without a
landscape block. The same header's `highlight` loads `lua-ul` with `[soul]`, which stopped LuaLaTeX (`\textul already defined`,
or an option clash) when a kit, the class or a `preamble.tex` had loaded soul or a bare lua-ul; pdfmd went on to XeLaTeX.

- `markup_header_pieces` (`lib/pdfmd_tex/markup.py`, a stand-in in `pdfmd.py`; `markup_header_args` gives it the Pandoc command so
  far) gives the guarded header when LaTeX of somebody else's may come before it: a chosen kit, a header file outside pdfmd's
  cache folder (`preamble.tex`, `-H`), `--template` or a defaults file, a `documentclass` other than article, report, book, the
  three KOMA classes, memoir and beamer (`STANDARD_CLASSES`). The guarded `landscape` loads pdflscape (or lscape, or the empty
  stand-in) only when `\landscape` and `\endlandscape` are not both defined; `::: landscape` writes `\begin{landscape}`, so it
  uses whichever environment there is. The guarded `highlight` loads lua-ul only when it is not loaded (bare, without `[soul]`,
  after soul) and, after a soul of somebody else's, sets pdfmd's colour inside `\pdfmdhl` only, so a kit's own `\hl` keeps its
  colour on pdfLaTeX and XeLaTeX. A document with nothing before the header gets it as before, byte for byte.

  HEAD, page 2 still rot 90. A `preamble.tex` with `\usepackage{soul}`, and one with `\usepackage{lua-ul}`: LuaLaTeX failed, now
  builds. Documents with string and mapping authors, `-t latex -s`: byte-identical.

  a CJK author's name brings; `pdfmd-pdfmeta-*.tex`) were taken for the user's, so such a document got the guarded header

## v3.33.62 — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `76d2dc0`. **A Typst older than 0.12 is refused as an engine, with one line that says so.** v3.33.58
had given such a Typst a branch of its own for the space between paragraphs (`pdfmd-typst-block-spacing`: `#show par: set
block(spacing: ...)` where 0.12's `par.spacing` is missing), never tested on a real one. That branch is gone
(`lib/pdfmd_paragraph`'s `typst_args` passes the value only, `pdfmd_lua/typst.lua` writes `#set par(spacing: ...)` only), and
pdfmd needs Typst 0.12 (`TYPST_MIN` in `lib/pdfmd_install`, a version fact: `par.spacing` and a `set document` in the body
are 0.12's). An older one is treated as the engine chain treats a missing one (`typst_too_old`):

- `-e typst` (and its alias `-e 6`, the `typst` family) stops before anything runs: "Typst 0.11.1 is older than 0.12, which
  pdfmd needs: update it (PATH-TO-IT; github.com/typst/typst/releases), or take it off PATH and run `pdfmd --install typst`"
  (a Typst on PATH wins over pdfmd's own, so the installer alone would not replace it); when the old one is pdfmd's own,
  "`pdfmd --install typst` puts a current one in its place".
- `-e typst,lualatex`: `NOTE  --engine: typst: Typst 0.11.1 is older ...; the next in the list is tried`, as for an engine
  that is not installed.
- The automatic chain keeps Typst in its list and passes it over when it gets there (`SKIP  doc.md: Typst 0.11.1 is older
  ...`), so a build that LaTeX makes asks Typst nothing.
- The version is `typst_version()`, whose `typst --version` is cached for the run (the build record asks the same), so a build
  with a current Typst starts no second process; asked only where Typst is named or reached.

- Checked through pdfmd with a fake `typst` on PATH that says `typst 0.11.1`: `-e typst` (`indent: true`): the line, exit 1,
  the fake never run (HEAD: Pandoc ran it with `-M pdfmd-typst-block-spacing=true`, and the build failed on it); `-e
  typst,lualatex`: the NOTE, then LuaLaTeX OK; no `-e`, a document whose `\undefinedcommandxyz` fails the three LaTeX engines:
  `SKIP ... Typst 0.11.1 is older ...`, then WeasyPrint OK. The real Typst 0.15.1 with `indent: true`: OK, no
  `block-spacing` in the command.
- Tests: `test_engine_chain` (alone, as an alias, in a list, a current one, none found, the automatic chain asks nothing,
  pdfmd's own Typst; through pdfmd with the fake: stops before it runs; fail at HEAD), `test_paragraph_spacing` (no version is
  asked) and `test_engine_filters` (the old rule's case removed). `test_engine_chain test_paragraph_spacing test_engine_filters
  test_calibre test_native test_browser_engine test_install_core_tex test_calibre_markdown test_office_latex test_split
  test_packaging test_docs_consistency test_setup`: 303 OK (7 skipped); the run's end check named another session's build in
  a temporary folder (counted then, fixed in 3.33.62b).
- README (the engine order) says so.

## v3.33.59 — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `901a2b9`. **Typst: the reference list's entries no longer overlap.** With a CSL whose
`<bibliography entry-spacing="0">` (APA 6th, among others) each entry's first line was printed on top of the previous entry's
last line, at every `linestretch`. Pandoc's Typst template turns entry-spacing N into `#show <refs>: set par(spacing: Nem)`,
and Typst measures that spacing edge to edge, from a line's baseline to the next line's cap height, where the line pitch inside
an entry is the leading plus that height. So 0 gave a pitch of the cap height alone (7.88 to 7.96 pt at 12 pt Times New
Roman; `measure[X].height` is 7.95 pt), and 1 gave 1em, closer than the lines of one entry once `linestretch` is above about
1.5 (19.88 pt between entries, 23.48 pt between lines at `linestretch: 2`). LaTeX's `CSLReferences` sets `\itemsep` to N x
`\baselineskip`: N lines added to the line pitch (measured, LuaLaTeX: 0 gives one pitch, 1 two).

- `pdfmd_lua/typst.lua` puts `#show: body => context { set par(spacing: par.leading + N * (par.leading +
  measure[X].height)); body }` at the top of the `refs` div (`par.leading` alone for 0): entry-spacing 0 sets the entries at
  the document's line spacing, 1 one line more, as in LaTeX. Inside the div, so an `--include-in-header` that replaces the
  header-includes does not drop it. Only for a whole N of 0 or more, where Pandoc's template writes a spacing: without the
  attribute, or with `2.5` (Pandoc writes none), the entries keep the paragraph spacing as before.
  `measure[X].height` is the height of a line (Typst's line box runs from `text.top-edge`, the cap height, to
  `text.bottom-edge`, the baseline: font metrics, so any glyph gives the same; a format fact, named `LINE_HEIGHT`).
- Checked through pdfmd (`pdftotext -bbox-layout`, the pitch at each entry boundary against the pitch inside an entry,
  three wrapped APA 6 entries at 12 pt): `linestretch` 1, 1.5, 2 with entry-spacing 0: 15.68/15.68, 19.58/19.58,
  23.48/23.48 (were 7.88 at each, overlapping); entry-spacing 1: 31.37, 39.17, 46.97 (two pitches; were 19.88). With
  `indent: true` and with `--paragraph-spacing 6pt` the same (the body's paragraph gap 29.48 with 6pt; the entries keep no
  first-line indent). The heading-to-first-entry gap is unchanged. A seven-page report with APA 6 (`linestretch: 2`, Times
  New Roman, Typst): pages 1 to 6 word for word in the same places, page 7 the same down to the end of the first entry,
  then each entry 23.53 pt below the last line (eight overlaps before, none after). `-t typst -s`: the one new line; with no
  CSL (Pandoc's default style, no entry-spacing) byte-identical to HEAD. `-r` (two parts, Typst): no overlap (two before).
  `--citeproc` comes before typst.lua on each Typst route (`-e typst`, the office pre-pass route, `-r`).
- Tests: `test_engine_filters` (the rule for 0, 2, 2.5, none and another div; a Typst PDF through pdfmd with entry-spacing 0
  and 1, the pitches measured); both fail at HEAD. `test_engine_filters test_paragraph_spacing test_office_latex
  test_engine_chain test_split test_packaging test_docs_consistency`: 132 OK.

## v3.33.58 — 2026-11-10

Pre-edit state: commit `27c75a2`. **The space between paragraphs is a setting, and `indent: true` drops it in Typst as in
LaTeX.** With `indent: true` Pandoc's LaTeX template leaves out the parskip package, so the next paragraph starts one line
below; Typst kept its own spacing (1.2em, 6 pt more than a line at 11 pt). And there was no way to set the gap.

- `indent: true`: `pdfmd_lua/typst.lua` adds `#set par(spacing: 0.65em)` beside the first-line indent (3.33.42): Typst's
  paragraph spacing becomes its line spacing. Typst measures both edge to edge, and the leading is the one Pandoc's template
  sets, `linestretch` x 0.65em (`linestretch: 1.5` gives `0.975em`; a `-V linestretch` first, as in the template).
  `TYPST_LEADING_EM = 0.65` is Typst's documented default leading, a format fact (named and commented in the filter).
- `pdfmd-options: {paragraph-spacing: 6pt}` (the document, its metadata files, the config, `--setup`) and `--paragraph-spacing
  LENGTH` for a run: what a paragraph break adds to the line spacing, a length (pt, mm, cm, in, em), `0` (any zero is `0pt`) or
  `auto`, the default (each engine's own, so nothing changes unless it is set). A bare number, a negative length or another
  unit stops the build with `... must be a length such as 6pt or 1em (pt, mm, cm, in, em), 0, or auto, not '6px'`, naming
  `--paragraph-spacing` or `pdfmd-options.paragraph-spacing`. A new package, `lib/pdfmd_paragraph`, reads it:
  - LaTeX and Beamer (the PDF route, `-t latex`/`beamer`, `-r`, the natbib/biblatex route): `\setlength{\parskip}{X}` in a
    header file of its own, after the template's parskip set-up.
  - Typst (`-e typst`, `-t typst`, `-r`): `-M pdfmd-paragraph-spacing=X`, and typst.lua writes `#set par(spacing: <leading> +
    X)`. Not `spacing: X` as such: Typst's spacing replaces the line gap where LaTeX's `\parskip` is added to it, so `0` would
    set paragraphs closer than lines (measured: 7.15 pt less than the line pitch at 11 pt) and `6pt` 1.15 pt closer than
    LaTeX's. With the leading added the same value gives the same gap on both. A Typst before 0.12 has no `par.spacing`:
    pdfmd says so (`pdfmd-typst-block-spacing`, only when the `typst` found is older; none found counts as current) and the
    filter writes `#show par: set block(spacing: ...)` (not tested here: the Typst on this machine is 0.15.1).
  - The HTML engines and `--to html` are not given it: pdfmd adds no style sheet of its own in one place there; the docs say
    a style sheet's `p { margin: ... }` sets theirs.
- `--setup` row (`options.paragraph-spacing`, with its UNSET words, a folder option) and `lib/pdfmd_setup/inventory.py`; the
  flag is in `--help output`; README (settings inside the document), `docs/recipes.md` (beside `indent`) and `pdfmd.py`'s opening docstring.

  11.0. With `indent: true`: default 0.0; 0.0 (Typst was 6.05 at HEAD), and `6pt`, `0`, `1em` as above, the second paragraph
  indented in both. `linestretch: 1.5` with `indent: true`: 0.0 on both. `-r` (both engines) and `citation-engine: natbib`
  with `0`: 0.0. The `-t latex -s` line comes after `\usepackage{parskip}` and after a discovered `preamble.tex`;

Pre-edit state: commit `29a31a0`. **An option Pandoc does not take stops the build once, with Pandoc's message.** `pdfmd doc.md
--no-such-flag` passes the option on to Pandoc (as it does every option pdfmd does not know), and Pandoc refused it; the engine
chain took that for an engine failure and tried every other engine (xelatex, pdflatex, typst, weasyprint, groff, edge, calibre,
soffice), each with a `WARN ... failed (Try pandoc --help ...); trying ...` line, before the same `FAIL`.

- Pandoc exits with 6 (its `PandocOptionError`) for a command line it refuses: an unknown option, one without its argument, a value
  it does not take (`--wrap=bogus`). `pandoc_refused_command` (`lib/pdfmd_tex`, beside `engine_failure_reason`) says so, and the
  engine loop stops there without a WARN; the `FAIL` line shows Pandoc's own message, as `--to html` always did. A refused
  `--pdf-engine` value (an older Pandoc that does not know the engine; also exit 6) still falls through to the next engine; an
  unknown option whose name starts with it (`--pdf-engines`) does not. An engine that does not suit the output format is exit 4
  in Pandoc 3.13, not 6. The other options pdfmd adds for one engine only are either `--pdf-engine-opt` values (Pandoc does not
  check them) or chosen by the Pandoc version (`--embed-resources`, the math option), so one engine's refusal is every engine's.
  Valid Pandoc options pass through as before (`--toc` builds; `--pdf-engine-opt=--nosuch` reaches lualatex, which only warns).
  `PANDOC_OPTION_ERROR = 6` is a constant: Pandoc's exit code, not a threshold.

  --no-such-flag.`, exit 1; `--wrap=bogus` and `--pdf-engines` the same with Pandoc's line.

## v3.33.18 — 2026-11-09

Pre-edit state: commit `53101da`. **In a `::: calc` div only the calculation lines lose their first-line indent; the prose between them keeps the document's.** A new value of `calc: {noindent: ...}`, `lines`, and the new default (the author, 2026-11-09).

- **The default changes.** Since 3.30.9 a `::: calc` div took the first-line indent off every paragraph inside it, so a sentence of explanation between two calculation lines was flush left as well, and the way round it was a `::: calc` div per line. Now a paragraph that holds a calculation line (an `{ans}`, `{subs}`, `{nosubs}`, `{upright:..}` or `{italic:..}` marker) gets `indent=false` on its own, and a paragraph of prose keeps the document's indent. A document built again looks different where its calc divs hold prose; `calc: {noindent: true}` (or `--calc-noindent`) gives the old look.
- The values: `lines` (the default), `true` (or `all`: every paragraph of the div, as before), `false` (the whole div keeps the document's indent). On the command line `--calc-noindent [lines|all]` (alone it means all, as before) and `--no-calc-noindent`; `PDFMD_CALC_NOINDENT` carries the same words to `-j` workers; the `--setup` row offers lines, on and off. An `indent=` or an `.indent` / `.noindent` class on the div still wins, and a nested `::: indent` / `::: noindent` div sets the paragraphs inside it: the paragraphs of the calc div itself are the only ones `lines` looks at.
- How: `lib/pdfmd_lua/calc.lua` wraps each such paragraph in a div with `indent=false` before it evaluates the div, and `lib/pdfmd_lua/indent.lua` turns that into what each writer has (a `\begingroup\setlength{\parindent}{0pt}` group in LaTeX, a `#[#set par(first-line-indent: 0pt)` block in Typst, `text-indent: 0pt` in HTML). In `pdfmd.py`, `calc_noindent_on()` became `calc_noindent_mode()` (lines, all or off) and the filter gets `-M pdfmd-calc-noindent=lines` or `=true`.
- Checked: a document with `indent: true` and a calc div holding two calculation lines, prose between them, a nested `::: noindent` paragraph and a `{=calc}` block, built to LaTeX, Typst, HTML, and to PDF with LuaLaTeX and with Typst, looked at in the rendered pages: the calculation lines flush left, the prose indented, the nested paragraph flush left. (Typst has no indent from `indent: true` itself; inside a `::: {indent=2em}` div it shows the same as LaTeX.) `--calc-noindent` gives one group around the whole div again; `--no-calc-noindent` none but the nested div's. Docs: the module docstring, `--help`, README's calc settings, `docs/recipes.md`, the `--setup` row. Tests: `test_calc` (114, one new: the lines default, `--calc-noindent lines`, all and off in LaTeX; the expected filter arguments say `lines`), `test_indent`, `test_split` and the always-run set (163) pass.

Nothing uses them yet; the next moves do.
- SPLIT.md, steps 4 and 6: a new package is re-exported plainly (it holds only the moved code); an existing package that does not load at start is deferred, and its move adds a build through the real call site to `split_check.py`, whose default builds may never reach it. `scripts/split_spec.py` reads tuple bindings (`ANSI_WIDTH_ENV, ANSI_COLOR_ENV, ANSI_LINKS_ENV = ...` showed as "not found").
- New `tests/test_split.py` (4 tests): the stand-in loads its module only on the first call and binds `core`; a deferred name is the package's own object; an unknown name is still an `AttributeError`; `import pdfmd` loads neither `pdfmd_serve`, `pdfmd_office`, `http.server` nor `ssl`. ## v3.32.54d — 2026-11-09

No shipped code (SPLIT.md); `PDFMD_VERSION` stays 3.32.54. Entry 3fi. **SPLIT.md is the verified plan for phase 1 of the split of `pdfmd.py`.** The first survey (2026-11-08) gave line ranges that overlapped (one group's range held another whole group), mixed topics and left out about 85 definitions; most groups were in two to thirteen separate places in the file. ## v3.32.43 — 2026-11-05

Pre-edit state: commit `81eac86`. Entry 3do. **`backup: {keep: N}` means what `pdfs: N` means, and `backups:` is a second spelling of `backup:`.** The author: "keep: 0 keeps all? then we shall make it consistent so 0 is now indeed 0 and negative is all; it will change current behaviour, but that is fine", and "backup: also has alias backups: right, to not frustrate anyone?".

- **`keep`: the newest N source copies; 0 none; a negative number every one** (also the words `all`, `none`, `off`). **The default is now negative (all), so a document that never sets `keep` behaves as before.** Only an explicit `keep: 0` changes: it meant all, it now means none. With 0 pdfmd makes no source copy and **deletes nothing that is already there** (setting a number to 0 must not destroy what was kept); the PDFs follow the same rule through `pdfs: 0`. `keep` and `pdfs` share one parser (`backup_count`), and a wrong value names its key (`pdfmd-options.backup.keep`).
- **`backups:`** is read wherever `backup:` is (front matter, metadata files, folder settings, the config file), field by field; where both are set in one place, `backup` wins.
- An empty `keep:` (or `keep: ~`) is no setting, as before (it must not read as `none`). The `--setup` row, the `--help` text and `tests/test_backup_keep.py` (8 checks) say so.
