- **One list.** The filters pdfmd puts on what a document says (the metadata that appends, `\md{}`, calc, the CSV tables, page breaks, indent, callouts and the other markup, table captions, line breaks, the title, the cover, raw pieces and diagrams, cross-references) were written out four times, once for each way a build reaches Pandoc (the PDF engines, the LaTeX route of `natbib`/`biblatex`, the other writers, the Office route). They are now `document_filter_args()` in `pdfmd.py`, and the four sites call it. The `--verbose` Pandoc command lines of 15 builds (html, docx, tex, latex, typst, odt, gfm, pdf with lualatex, typst, weasyprint and soffice, natbib, a part, a part to html) are byte for byte what they were. `serve_live_filters` (3.32.40's own list of one filter) calls the same function: a syntax added there shows in every writer and in the live view with nothing else to do. A test fails if a build site writes one of these filters itself again.
- **What the live view needed besides.** Pandoc's `sourcepos` (the block positions the source mirror reads) wraps every word in a span, every block without attributes in a div, and splits `{=}` into three words, which hid the pairs the filters look for: calc's `` `1/2`{=} `` and the paragraphs inside a `::: calc` div stayed as typed. `pdfmd_lua/sourcepos.lua`, the live view's one filter of its own, runs first and puts the document back as the reader gives it (the wrappers inside another block go, neighbouring words are one again); the blocks of the document itself keep theirs, which carry the positions. Calc, callouts, page breaks and CSV tables now show in the live view; `Core(filters=...)` is called with the document and its metadata files, and a text that is not saved yet is read from the text itself, not from the file on disk: what a filter reads of the document (its own settings and those of the folders above it) it reads from a copy of the text beside the document (a hidden `.pdfmd-live-NAME`, removed when the render is done; the file itself when it already says that text; a folder that cannot be written to gets a copy elsewhere and loses its folder settings). What pdfmd says about a filter it did not run comes back as a warning of the render, not as a line on the server's console.
- **Still as typed, because the reader is not the build's:** citations (`[@key]`), `: caption` lines under a pipe table and what builds on them (`\cref`); the live view reads CommonMark (positions) and a build reads pandoc's Markdown. The remaining decision is the earlier one (a second route for the live view, entry 3do).
- Measured on real parts of a lab report (25 KB of text): 0.1 to 0.4 s a render, the plain pandoc 0.12 s.

## v3.32.34 — 2026-11-04

Pre-edit state: commit `9e96af6`. `[tables]`, entry 3fa. **Cell tags keep a table's natural width; the limits are written down.** Found by reviewing v3.32.31-33 before any push.

- **The bug (from v3.32.31, unreleased).** A tag is longer than what it replaces (`&c&` 3 characters, `<pc hc>` 7; the carrier of an attribute line 20 to 60). Pandoc reads a pipe table whose longest source line is over 72 characters as a table of widths taken from the separator's dashes, so a small table with unequal dashes that was natural before its tags could be stretched across the page. The first canonical tag (60 characters) did exactly that; shortening it was not enough for a table near the limit.
- **The fix.** `celltags.py` cuts the padding of the rows it rewrites; when a line that was under 72 would still cross it, the carrier gets the word `nw` (`<pt nw ...>`) and the table's column widths are reset to the default before `table_width.lua` measures it (a few lines in its `rebalance`, which is why this entry names that file) and in `cellalign.lua` for the writers that filter does not run for. A table that was over 72 before its tags is left as Pandoc read it. The 72 is Pandoc's own `--columns` default, a constant in `celltags.py` (`PANDOC_COLUMNS`) and not a setting.
- **Checked.** Cross-references to a table rebuilt as a `longtblr`: with `pandoc-crossref` running, the caption and `label=` carry over and `\ref` resolves (built and compiled). The native (no-Pandoc) tier prints the author's own text (the arrows, `&c&`, the `{...}` line) and never the internal `<pc>` / `<pt>` tags. README: the limits (a rebuilt table is raw LaTeX to later filters and to `table-keep`; Beamer untested; `cell-align: off` also switches the attribute line off).
- **Tests.** The tests that depended on Pandoc 3.13's exact output are looser (the LaTeX `\multicolumn`, the HTML style) or gated (`needs_pandoc(3, 1, 13)` for the Typst spans), since CI also runs Pandoc 3.1.3; +3 tests for the natural width.

## v3.32.33 — 2026-11-04

Pre-edit state: commit `7cb62bc`. `[tables]`, entry 3fa, step 3 of 3. **A table's attribute line: widths, heights and alignment tiers.** The author: "choosing arbitrary cell width and height ... none is easily achievable".

- **The line.** `{widths="3cm * 15%" row2.height=1.8cm col2.align=l,m valign=m}` right under a table (or under its `Table:` caption). Settings: `width` / `widths` (a length in cm, mm, in, pt or em, a percentage, `*` for a share of what is left, `auto`), `height` (the least height of a row: `row3.height`, or `height` for every row; `ht` in tabularray is a minimum, a taller cell still grows its row), `align` (the words of a cell tag) and `valign`, each for the table, `colN.` or `rowN.`. A problem in it (`col9.width` in a table of three columns, a width that is not a length) is a `WARN  cell-tags` and left out; a braced line with no `key=value` (`{#tbl:x}`) is not read.
- **How.** The pre-pass cuts the line out and writes its settings, short, into the first header cell as `<pt c2w=3cm r2ht=1.8cm v=m>` (a block between a table and its `Table:` caption would cut the tie Pandoc makes, so the carrier is a cell). LaTeX draws such a table as a `longtblr` (the vertical-alignment machinery of v3.32.32, now also for widths and heights): `Q[l,wd=3cm]`, `X[1,l]` for `*`, `Q[r,wd=0.15\linewidth]`, `row{2}={ht=1.8cm}`, `width=` for the table. HTML gets percentage widths as `<col style="width: 20%">` (the AST's column widths), a `height` and a `vertical-align` style per cell. Absolute widths outside LaTeX, and these settings in Typst and Word, are not drawn yet. The Markdown writers write the line back in its own spelling.
- **Tiers.** For a cell, most specific first: its tag, its row, its column, the column's `:--:`, the table's `align=` / `valign=`, then the defaults of the two new options. A column's `:--` is above a table-wide `align=` (a first version had it the other way round).
- **New options** `table-align` (left, center, right) and `table-valign` (top, middle, bottom), `pdfmd-options` and `--setup` rows (Tables); a word that is not one of them stops the build. `table-valign` draws every table of a LaTeX build through tabularray. The `NOTE` without tabularray now covers widths and heights too.
- `tests/test_celltags.py` (+14: the parser, the carrier and the caption, the two orders, a line that is not one, the LaTeX keys, HTML, Markdown reading it again, the option tiers, the stop on a wrong word).

## v3.32.32 — 2026-11-04

Pre-edit state: commit `5f54ef4`. `[tables]`, entry 3fa, step 2 of 3. **Vertical alignment of a table cell** (`t`, `m`, `b` in a cell tag: `&t&`, `&mc&`, `<m>`, `&merge-up,bottom&`). The author: "centering (on x and y separately or both together), top bottom left down alignment".

- **LaTeX.** A row has one baseline in LaTeX, so Pandoc's `longtable` cannot align one cell. A table with a vertical letter is rebuilt by `cellalign.lua` as a `longtblr` (tabularray) from Pandoc's own table model: columns and widths (the table-width filter's), header rows (`rowhead`, repeated on every page), spans, per-cell alignment, caption and label (a table without a caption gets `caption={},entry=none,label=none`, otherwise tabularray prints an empty "Table N:"). The package goes in a header file of pdfmd's own (`tblr_header_args`; a filter's `header-includes` is dropped by every header file of pdfmd's) with tabularray's "Continued on next page" and "(Continued)" templates emptied, as Pandoc's tables have none. A table with no vertical letter is untouched.
- **tabularray's words.** Its `t` and `b` are baseline alignments (a "top" cell beside a "middle" one drew misaligned in the first spike); its true top, middle and bottom are `h`, `m`, `f`, which is what the filter writes, and every cell of such a table starts as `h` (`cells={valign=h}`).
- **HTML** gets `style="vertical-align: ..."`. Typst and Word do not draw it yet (a `#align(horizon)[...]` wrapper made Typst swallow the cell, so it was not kept).
- **No tabularray** (`kpsewhich` cannot find it, `tabularray_available()`): the filter is told `-M pdfmd-tblr=off`, the vertical letters are ignored in a LaTeX build and one NOTE says so; the build goes on.
- `tests/test_celltags.py` (+7: the longtblr keys, a table with and without a caption in one document, spans with vertical letters, the PDF build, HTML, the fallback).

## v3.32.31 — 2026-11-04

Pre-edit state: commit `c49cfce`. `[tables]`, entry 3fa. **Merged cells in pipe tables, and cell tags in any spelling.** The author: "can we enhance tables, like very? ... merging tables, choosing arbitrary cell width and height, centering (on x and y separately or both together), top bottom left down alignment --- none is easily achievable". Decided over several rounds of design (syntax, delimiters, clashes); this is the first of three steps (spans, then vertical alignment, then widths and heights).

- **Merging.** A cell that is `<<`, `>>`, `^^` or `vv` (bare, or inside a `&...&` tag) belongs to the neighbour on that side; the arrow points at the cell that holds the content, chains are followed, the region must be a rectangle (a WARN and no merge otherwise), an empty cell is never merged by itself, a covered cell's text is added to the merged cell on a new line with a WARN, and a header cell that spans rows takes the body rows it reaches into the header. LaTeX gets `\multirow` / `\multicolumn`; HTML, Typst and Word the spans of Pandoc's table model.
- **Tags anywhere in the cell**, in three spellings: `&...&` (the recommended one, takes letters, words and arrows), `<...>` (letters and words, `<br>` / `<tr>` / `<tt>` stay HTML, `<b>` and `<center>` only without a closing tag) and a bare arrow as the whole cell; `{...}` and `«...»` are opt-in. Letters in any order and case (`mc` = `cm` = `cc`; a lone `c` is still horizontal), comma, space or nothing between them, full words (`top`, `centre`, `merge-up`) matched without `-`, `_` and `.`. Code, math and a backslash-escaped tag are left alone; a tag must stand apart.
- **New setting `table-tag-brackets`** (a list of `angle`, `amp`, `brace`, `guillemet`; default `angle, amp`), a `--setup` row. `cell-align: off` now switches every cell tag off.
- **How.** A pre-pass on a temporary copy (`lib/pdfmd_tables/celltags.py`, like `table-ascii`) reads every spelling and writes one short canonical raw tag per cell (`<pc c2 r2 hc vm>`, `<pc xl>`); `cellalign.lua` reads only that, sets `col_span` / `row_span`, drops covered cells and moves header rows. The tag is short on purpose: Pandoc turns a pipe table whose source line is longer than its column limit into a full-width table of dash-proportional columns, which a long tag did to a small table in the first try. The filter still runs after the table-width filter, which measures the table as written.
- **Changed behaviour.** `<l>`, `<c>`, `<r>` are found anywhere in a cell (before: only at its start). The Markdown writers write a cell tag back as `&c&` (before: the raw `<c>`), so the output reads again. Vertical letters (`t`, `m`, `b`) are read and carried but not drawn yet (the next patch).
- `tests/test_celltags.py` (35 tests: tokens, spellings, clashes, merging, real builds to LaTeX, HTML, Typst, Word and Markdown), `test_cellalign.py` adjusted for the two changes above.

## v3.32.30 — 2026-11-04

Pre-edit state: commit `3b179af`. **A kit's front matter survives every header file (`headers_as_metadata`).** The author, after `pdfmd '#20'` on an APA 7 paper stopped with "There's no line here to end": "let's make it more robust ... the same issue may repeat with other kits".

- **The bug.** Pandoc puts `--include-in-header` files and `header-includes` in one template variable and the files win. A kit's Lua filter writes its front-matter commands (apa7's `\authorsnames`, `\authorsaffiliations`, `\shorttitle` ...) into `header-includes`, so any header file of pdfmd's dropped them: `\maketitle` stopped. A full build passed no header file and worked; a partial build (`report#methods`) passes the labels of the whole document as two, so it failed, and so would a full build of a document with a code block, a raw `\includegraphics` or a callout. All nine kits write their preamble this way.
- **The fix.** For a LaTeX build (a LaTeX PDF engine, or `-t latex` / `beamer`) that has a header file and a Lua filter that is not pdfmd's own, `headers_as_metadata` takes the header files off the command and hands them over as `-M pdfmd-header-file-N=PATH`. Two new filters do the rest: `header_snap.lua` (first) records what `header-includes` holds, `header_merge.lua` (last) makes `header-includes` the files in their order plus whatever the other filters added, in front of the packages header. Nothing else about the header files changes (`keep_header_includes`, `hoist_code_header`, the kit header all still work on the files). A build without a foreign filter, or a non-LaTeX build, runs exactly as before.
- Run at the three places where the finished command runs: the PDF engine closure, `-t latex` and the native-bibliography `.tex`.

## v3.32.29o — 2026-11-04

Pre-edit state: commit `91ded94`. Entry 3do; `gui/` only, no shipped pdfmd code, so no `PDFMD_VERSION` bump. **Colophon 0.2.14: File > Export As.** The author: "let's implement export into files, like main ones: standalone markdown, pdf (selectable engines, maybe dropdown in dropdown expandable), docx, html, and others dropdown with everything available via pdfmd".

- **File > Export As** (`Editor/Export.swift`, `Editor/ExportController.swift`): Markdown (standalone) is `pdfmd FILE --merge -o OUT`; PDF is Automatic or one engine in a submenu per family (LaTeX, Typst, HTML and browsers, Others), each `-t pdf -e ENGINE`; Word and HTML; and **Others**, with Beamer slides as a PDF, grouped (documents, slides, e-books, web, plain text and Markdown, markup, XML and data, pictures): 108 rows in all, each one a pdfmd command line and nothing else (the app converts nothing). The table is data: the menu, `colophon export --list [--json]` and the smoke test read it. Every Pandoc writer is either in it or named with the reason it is not (`ExportTable.notOffered`), and the smoke test fails for a new one.
- **The flow**: the document is saved first (pdfmd needs its folder), a Save panel proposes the name with the format's extension (`NAME.assembled.md` for the standalone Markdown, as pdfmd names it), pdfmd runs through the same run code as a build (the file and `-t … -o OUT` go to the shell as arguments, never into the script, so a path with a quote stays whole), the window's subtitle says how it went, a failure opens the build log. It refuses an output that is the document itself, and it does not run beside a build (either one says so).
- **Your own "pdfmd options for a build" are used too**, without any `-t` or `-o` of yours: pdfmd refuses `--merge` together with a target, and `-t html` kept there would have made HTML in a `.pdf`. Every export writes its own `-t`, also for PDF (an explicit target beats the extension of `-o`).
- **An export is not a build**: it does not touch "the last build", never lands in the preview pane and never opens a PDF viewer. It counts as done when pdfmd exits 0 and either its `OK  a.md > OUT` line names the file or the file is there and newer than the start (a stale file of an earlier export is no success).
- **Engines that are missing are greyed**: `pdfmd --check-dependencies` is read once, the first time the menu is looked at (about a second); a `MISS` greys the item, an engine it does not list (the browsers) stays enabled. Setting `exportReveal` (default off) shows the file in Finder when done.
- **`colophon export FILE FORMAT [--engine E] [-o OUT]`**: the same without the window (`colophon render FILE ...` with the table's words), so a script or an agent writes the files the menu writes; `--list` and `--list --json` print the table.

## v3.32.29b — 2026-11-04

Pre-edit state: commit `f8fde88`. Entry 3do; `gui/` only, no shipped pdfmd code, so no `PDFMD_VERSION` bump. **pdfmd Edit 0.2.1: the PDF viewer no longer reloads itself over and over.** The author: "the pdf viewer in its current state is unusable. zooming doesn't work properly, navigation using thumbnails is broken ... fast scroll ... lagged", then "scrolling is now dead".

- Cause: `presentedItemDidChange` also fires when only the file's access time moves. Every reload reads the file, so it moved the access time, so it reported a change, so it reloaded again, about every 1.5 s. Each reload swaps in a new PDFView and puts the old place and zoom back, which undid the scroll, the thumbnail jump and the zoom, and rebuilt the thumbnails. The file's modification time, status time and attributes did not change (checked with `stat`), which is why it was hard to see.
- Fix (`gui/Sources/PDF/PDFViewer.swift`): `FileStamp` (modification time to the nanosecond, size, inode) is taken before the file is read; a change report whose stamp equals the shown one is ignored. Taken before the read, so a write landing during the read is still seen next.
- **The sidebar's empty strip:** hiding the thumbnails hid the view but the page area kept its place, leaving a dark empty box; the split view is laid out again (`adjustSubviews`) when the sidebar is hidden.
- Tests: `--smoke-pdf` (now 48 checks) has "a change of the access time alone does not reload" (the old test counted reloads with `>=` and never looked for spurious ones) and "hidden thumbnails leave no empty strip" / "shown thumbnails make room again" (the old one only looked at `isHidden`). New developer tools: `PDFMDEDIT_TRACE=1` writes a timestamped trace (place changes, file notifications with the file's times, main-thread stalls over `PDFMDEDIT_TRACE_STALL` ms) to `/tmp/pdfmdedit-trace.log`; `--live-pdf FILE [thumb|scroll|zoom|hide|all]` runs thumbnail clicks, wheel flicks, zooms and the sidebar toggle in a real window without taking focus. It did not reproduce the loop (an inactive app gets no thumbnail clicks, and the loop needs the system's own access-time reports); the trace did.

Pre-edit state: commit `7720630`. Entry 3ee, step 4(c). **Obsidian's links between notes are written as the text they show, and `<u>` is underlined in every writer.**

- **`markup: underline`**, a new markup kind (on in the `pdfmd` and `obsidian` flavours, like the others): `<u>..</u>` and `<ins>..</ins>` become Pandoc's Underline, so LaTeX gets `\ul`, Typst `#underline`, Word and OpenDocument an underlined run, HTML `<u>`; the Markdown family keeps the tags. Before, LaTeX, Typst and Word dropped the tags and printed the text plain. `==highlight==` was already a markup kind and needed no change.
- **Fix found on the way:** the LaTeX header of `highlight` loaded `soul`, which clashes with the `lua-ul` that Pandoc's template loads under LuaTeX for any underline (`Command \ul already defined`; lualatex fell back to xelatex). Under LuaTeX the header now loads `lua-ul` with its own `\highLight`; the highlight still renders pale yellow (checked in a PDF).
- Tests: `tests/test_wikilinks.py` (6: the transform, what is left alone, whole builds as HTML, LaTeX and Typst); `test_markup_callouts.py` lists the new kind.

## v3.32.18 — 2026-11-03

Pre-edit state: commit `cfd403f` (the split of the report and batch modes into `pdfmd_report` and `pdfmd_batch` is `e308bde`, v3.32.13). Kept in 3.32. Not pushed.

**A report (`-r`) is now built by the build of one document, and the titles of its files are chapter headings.** The PDF branch of the report was an old, stripped copy of the single-document engine loop: it chose no document font (so `≥ ′ ≈` came out of Latin Modern as `Missing character`), ignored `-f/--font`, and lacked the font retry, `citation-engine: natbib|biblatex` (citeproc silently), the Typst font path, the style sheets for HTML-based engines, the table-width note, the cache route and more.

- **`pdfmd-options: report-build: route|patch`** (default `route`; `--setup` row `options.report-build`). `route` hands `convert_one()` the first file and the others as its parts (`extra_inputs`, as a parts-mode scaffold does), so a report gets all that a document gets and prints the same `DEFAULTS` line (the README's `margin 1in, font STIX Two Text` example is true now). The report keeps its own: the files and their order, the metadata found for the folder, `book.EXT`, a stamp, backup and attached source for every chapter (`REPORT_BUILD` in `pdfmd.py`), the `OK file` / `SKIP` / `REPORT` lines. The front matter of the later files is no longer merged into the book's (a `NOTE` names the keys one of them sets that the report does not use). `patch` keeps the report's own Pandoc command over the list of files, now with the document font, the math font and `--font`, and the titles; it has no font retry, cache route or the other single-document steps. `--stop-at markdown` (the assembled Markdown) is unchanged and does not use either.
- **`pdfmd-options: report-titles: chapters|first|last`** (default `chapters`; `--setup` row `options.report-titles`). With two or more files that have a `title:`, `chapters` makes each title a level-1 heading (a `\chapter` in the report class), puts the file's `subtitle:` (and its `author:` and `date:` when they differ from the book's) in a line under it, and moves the file's own headings down one level (a setext heading becomes an ATX one; code blocks are left alone; a first line that repeats the title is not printed twice). The first file's title and subtitle leave its front matter, so the book has a title page only if a metadata file sets a title. `first` keeps the first title as the book's and drops the later; `last` makes the last title the book's. One titled file: nothing changes. The work is done on the Markdown text, in hidden copies handed to Pandoc (`pdfmd_report/titles.py`), so it is the same for every reader and writer.
- **A report is chapters** (the author, on the first look at the PDF: the headings were `\section`s, "it looks like an article with all headings demoted"; "shouldn't report be the default class?"). A PDF or LaTeX `-r` build now uses `documentclass: report` and `--top-level-division=chapter` when no document class is named by the files, the metadata files or `-V`, so each level-1 heading is a `\chapter` on a new page with a large title, and the file titles of `report-titles: chapters` are chapters, their own headings sections. A named `book`, `report`, `memoir` or KOMA class is kept; a class without chapters (`article`) is kept and a `NOTE` says a level-1 heading is a section. Both builds, any `report-titles`. No new key: `documentclass:` is the setting.
- The zipapp builder (`scripts/build_zipapp.py`) now lists `pdfmd_batch` and `pdfmd_report`, the two packages of the split (v3.32.13); without them a zipapp could not import pdfmd. `tests/test_packaging.py` caught it.

An image path relative to a chapter in a subfolder is still not found, as before.

The words of `priority`, and their order, are settings.

- **`ranking`**: classes of words on a ladder (`classes: {fruit: {words: [cherry, banana], above: numbers}}`: banana beats cherry, every fruit beats every number, `final` still beats them all), `ladder:` (a nested list is one level), `names: family | folder | off` (whether an inferred `final` beats an unrelated document: the author's "let's make it adjustable"), `by:` (what settles equal priority: `newest`, `oldest`, `name`; `[priority]` makes a tie the error of 3.32.9 again, `[newest]` ignores priority). A class takes `ordered: false`, `degrees`, `exclude`, `names: false`, `above:` / `below:`; a word may hold `{n}`. YAML's `names: off` (read as `false`) works, and `by` may be a comma list (`priority, oldest`), which is what the setup row stores.
- **Where it is read, nearest first**: the documents' own `pdfmd-options: {ranking: ...}` and a metadata file named after one (classes and ladder only; `by`, `names` and `inherit` are the folder's: a WARN), then folder by folder from theirs upward `.pdfmd/ranking.yaml` > the folder's `metadata.yaml` > the folder settings' `options.ranking`, then the global `ranking.yaml` (beside the config file) and the config's `options.ranking`. `inherit: false` stops the climb. A nearer `ladder`/`names`/`by` replaces a farther one, classes merge by name. Nothing is read, or parsed, until bare `pdfmd` has several documents to choose from, so a broken file never spoils another build.
- **Two documents that define a class (or the ladder) differently**: a WARN naming both; the newer one's is used. **Mistakes** (a word in two classes, an unknown class on the ladder, a bad `above:`) stop the choice with the file that defined it; a class on no ladder is a WARN and its words are ignored.
- **`--setup`**: two rows, *Equal priority, when bare pdfmd must choose a document* and *Names that rank versions of a document*, also in a folder's setup; `pdfmd_setup/inventory.py` lists `ranking.by` and `ranking.names` as rows and `ranking.ladder` / `ranking.classes` as left out on purpose (a file's lists). ## v3.32.8 — 2026-11-03

Pre-edit state: commit `1d992bd`. `[kits]`, entry 3et UPDATE 2 (the author: "let's do it. no-auto geometry"). Kept in 3.32. Not pushed.

A kit can take pdfmd's own margin, font and table-width defaults over with `no-auto:` in its `.kit` file.

- **The key**: `no-auto: [margin]` (a word or a list of `margin`, `mainfont`, `monofont`, `mathfont`, `font`, `tablewidth`). Before, a class kit had to write `geometry: " "` into its metadata to stop the automatic `geometry:margin=...` from clashing with the class's own page; now the kit says what it means, and the metadata can stay about the document.
- **Where it ranks**: under the command line, the document and the folders' files, over the config file (the same place a kit's metadata has). So a document can turn the default back on with `pdfmd-options: {auto: {margin: on}}`, and `--no-auto` and `-y` still mean what they meant. Applied to a single document and to a report or book (`-r`).
- **What a kit cannot name**: a kit is chosen from the layers and from the files pdfmd found, so it cannot switch off the finding of metadata, Lua filters, preambles or kits themselves; those kinds, and `true` for everything, are a WARN naming the kind and are ignored.
- **Not before**: an older pdfmd reads the key as an unknown one (a WARN) and goes on, so a kit that has it still builds there.
- The kits' own `active_kits` cache is keyed on the two `--no-auto` kinds that decide the kit search (`kit`, `kpsewhich`) instead of the whole list, so one run makes one choice of kits, and prints a kit's warnings once, whatever else is switched off.
- `pdfmd --kits NAME` shows the kit's `no-auto`. The module docstring now has a short Kits paragraph (it had none), the README's Kits section the key and its ranking.
- Tests: `tests/test_kit_no_auto.py`, through pdfmd itself (a real build with a kit that has no `geometry:`).

## v3.32.7 — 2026-11-03

Pre-edit state: commit `d14c00a`. `[kits]`, entry 3et UPDATE 1 (the author: "make it possible for `pdfmd --install kit` to fetch an arbitrary git repo ... it'll look at all folders of it so nulabreport, which has `.kit` at root, and this one, pdfmd-kits, which has kits in child dirs, would work"). Kept in 3.32. Not pushed.

`pdfmd --install kit:SOURCE` installs the kits of any repository.

- **Sources**: `owner/repo` (GitHub, its default branch; the tarball over https, no git needed), `owner/repo@REF` (a tag, branch or commit), `#NAME` after either picks one kit, any git URL (https, ssh, scp-like; `git clone --depth 1` with only the https, ssh and file transports, `ext::` refused), `file:///path` (a local git repository, committed state), `./x` `~/x` `/x` (a folder, copied as it is), and a bare `NAME` (a kit of that name in the repositories of `kit-sources`). Plain `http://` and `git://` are refused. `pdfmd --install kit` alone lists the installed kits; `pdfmd --uninstall kit:NAME` removes one.
- **What it finds**: a folder with `.kit` or `NAME.kit` is a kit; the repository root first, then every folder below it down to `kit-search-depth` (3) levels, hidden folders skipped, and a kit's own sub-folders are the kit's, never searched. So a repository that is one kit (the root shape of a package like nulabreport) and one with a kit per folder (a collection) both work. Each kit is checked with the kit loader; a faulty one is skipped with a WARN and the rest installed.
- **Where it goes**: `kits/NAME/` beside the config file (kit discovery already reads it), the whole kit folder, with `.pdfmd-install.json` (source, ref, commit, SHA-256 of the archive, path in the repository, date). `pdfmd --kits` shows where an installed kit came from. Installing again updates it (a staged copy, then a swap); a folder there that pdfmd did not install is never replaced; a kit of another source needs `--yes`.
- **Safe by construction**: nothing of the repository is run (no script, no hook, no kit Lua filter). The archive is read as data: a name that leaves the folder stops the install, links, devices and fifos are dropped, and the files and bytes are capped by `kit-install-max-files` (5000) and `kit-install-max-mb` (200). The install lists the kits that carry a Lua filter and says to read it: pdfmd runs it when a document selects the kit.
- **Settings** (`options:` of the config file, read at install time, no `--setup` row; the inventory lists them as omitted): `kit-search-depth`, `kit-install-max-mb`, `kit-install-max-files`, `kit-sources` (the repositories a bare name is looked for in).
- New module `pdfmd_kits/install.py` (pure; the downloader is handed in), `install_kits()` and `uninstall_kit()` in `pdfmd.py`, `kit` in `INSTALL_KINDS`.

## v3.32.6 — 2026-11-03

Pre-edit state: commit `f528e53`. `[kits]`, entry 3et (the author: "yes, follow pdfmd repo rules"). Kept in 3.32 as the author asked on 2026-11-02, though `CLAUDE.md` still names the kits line 3.31.x. Not pushed.

A kit's folders reach Tectonic.

- **The bug**: a kit puts its folder and its `carry:` folders on `TEXINPUTS`, which Tectonic does not read. With `-e tectonic` a kit that ships a LaTeX class (the apa7 kit of the kits repository, a class with its `config/` files) was never loaded: Tectonic built, without a word, with the copy of that class in its own bundle, or failed when its bundle had none. Found with a copy of the class that stops when it is loaded: xelatex stopped, Tectonic built.
- **The fix**: for the engine `tectonic`, each chosen kit's folder and every folder under the `carry:` entries that are folders go to Tectonic as `-Zsearch-path=DIR` (`tectonic_search_folders()`; the option names one folder, not a tree, so a carried tree is listed folder by folder, hidden folders left out). The Pandoc route passes them as `--pdf-engine-opt=-Zsearch-path=DIR`; the direct route (`.tex` files, drawn fragments) gets them through the environment `tex_search_env()` already builds (`PDFMD_TECTONIC_SEARCH`) and `latex_engine_command()`. Other engines and a document with no kit are unchanged. Needs a Tectonic that has `-Z search-path` (0.17 has it).
- Checked through pdfmd itself: the marker copy now stops under `-e tectonic` and the real apa7 kit builds; xelatex and lualatex were never affected.
- Tests: `tests/test_kit_texinputs.py` (the folders one by one, no hidden folder, no walk of the kit's whole folder, nothing without a kit, the command line of the direct route for Tectonic only).
- README: the paragraph "A kit needs no install" says it. No new setting.

## v3.32.5 — 2026-11-02

Pre-edit state: commit `b5cd684`. Entry 3eo, step 2a of the Obsidian flavour line (the author: "any Pandoc or whatever detected syntax switches the reader, unless those are like examples in fenced code blocks"). Not pushed.

- **No more "gfm leaves X as text" NOTE: pdfmd acts on what it finds.** A file with no front matter was read as gfm and, when it used `H~2~O`, `x^2^`, `{#id}` attributes, raw LaTeX or `:::` divs, a NOTE said gfm printed them as text. Now a table of detectors (`READER_NEEDS`, `reader_needs()`) decides, and each syntax needs one of two things: an extension Pandoc accepts on gfm, which is added to the reader (`gfm+subscript`, `+superscript`, `+attributes+bracketed_spans`, `+fenced_divs`, `+definition_lists`, `+fancy_lists`, `+raw_attribute`; the definition-list and `.csv` div cases were added on need before), or Pandoc's own Markdown reader, which the file is switched to (`^[inline footnotes]`, raw LaTeX, grid tables, simple tables, `(@)` example lists, as `@citations`, Org captions and `\md{}` already did). `--verbose` says which syntax decided: `reading as gfm+subscript (it uses subscripts (H~2~O))`, or `it uses raw LaTeX (...), which gfm cannot read; keeping the default markdown reader`.
- **Only prose is looked at**: fenced code, inline code, math (`$..$`, `$$..$$`; `$5 or $10` is not math) and HTML comments are taken out first, so an example of the syntax in a code block changes nothing. The line that opens a fence is the one exception (a fence with attributes, ```` ```{.smiles} ````, needs `+attributes`). Lettered and Roman-numeral lists count only as two items in a row (`a.` `b.`, `(i)` `(ii)`): `I. Introduction` alone stays text, as in GFM. Not looked for: indented code blocks, line blocks, multiline tables, inline `^x^` inside words (listed in the notes).
- **Cost, accepted by the author**: Pandoc's Markdown reader sizes pipe-table columns differently from gfm (the reason gfm was chosen); a file with raw LaTeX or an inline footnote and no front matter now gets that reader, so its tables size as they do in a file with front matter.
- Removed with it: `reader_notice()`, `gfm_blind_spots()`, `GFM_BLIND_SPOTS`, `FENCE_ATTRIBUTES`, `has_definition_list()` (the table replaces them); the NOTE is gone from the output.
- Tests: `tests/test_reader.py`: the old blind-spot tests became `ReaderNeeds` (the extension each syntax needs, what only Pandoc's reader reads, code and math and comments not counting, a fence's attributes, lettered lists) and the command-line tests (nothing said but under `-v`, the extension added and `<sub>` in the output, a switch to Pandoc's reader for an inline footnote and for raw LaTeX, the same syntax in a code block changes nothing). Checked through the whole `pdfmd` on the three notes of the Obsidian test vault (all read as plain gfm, nothing to add) and on small files.
- README: the "It decides per document" paragraph and the `READER` row say what is added and what switches.

Now only a metadata file of the document (beside it, `-y`, a folder's) counts. Measured against `pandoc -f markdown -t json` for 14 shapes. About twenty other places in `pdfmd.py` read a front-matter block with their own regex (`papersize`, margins, `pdfmd-options` ...); they all require a closing line, so they differ from this only for a file that opens with a rule and has another rule later. Left as they are, listed in the notes.

A document with front matter (every `nulabreport` report has some) is untouched. ## v3.32.1 — 2026-11-02

Pre-edit state: commit `c52dd09`. Entry 3en (the review of two research reports on Markdown-to-PDF pain points; the author: "diagram limit on at 120 s. the setting --- yes, and document it").

A diagram tool that never answered hung the build with no message: a stub `mmdc` that sleeps was still being waited for after 60 s. `pandoc.pipe`, which `pdfmd_lua/diagram.lua` ran the tools with, has no time limit.

- `diagram-timeout` (`pdfmd-options` key, config key, `--setup` row "Time limit of one diagram tool run" under Checks and limits): seconds one run of `mmdc`, `dot`, `d2`, or of the `rsvg-convert` / `inkscape` that converts their SVG, may take. Default 120, ON. `0`: no diagram is drawn (the fences stay as code, one WARN naming the setting; it overlaps `--no-auto diagrams`, kept so the value means what `soffice-timeout: 0` means). A negative number: no limit, and no runner.
- New `pdfmd_lua/limited_run.py`, started by the filter under the limit with the interpreter pdfmd runs on (so no `timeout` command is needed, which macOS and Windows lack): it passes standard input and output through as bytes (a picture written to standard output stays intact), leaves the tool's error output where it was, and when the time is up stops the tool with every process it started (a process group; `taskkill /T` on Windows), prints a marker and exits 124. 127 for a missing program.
- The filter: a stopped tool leaves its diagram as code with a WARN that says which program did not finish in how many seconds and names the setting (`--strict` makes it an error, like any undrawable diagram), and the tool is not tried again in the build, with one WARN for the first skipped fence: a browser that cannot start would otherwise cost the limit once per diagram. A stopped `dot` is not asked a second time for an SVG to convert. Nothing from a stopped run reaches the cache.
- Known cost, not fixed: the Word and OpenDocument route runs Pandoc twice, so there a hung tool costs the limit twice (each run remembers on its own).
- `diagram_timeout_from()` and `diagram_timeout_for()` (the document's key, its metadata files', the config's); the filter gets `pdfmd-diagram-timeout`, `-python` and `-runner`, or `pdfmd-diagram-off`, in the metadata map it already had.
- `tests/test_diagram_timeout.py` (6 tests: the value as seconds, a document's own limit, bytes through the runner, exit code and error output through the runner, a run stopped with its child, a missing program) and four in `tests/test_diagrams.py` (a hanging `dot` is stopped and the second fence does not start it again, nothing in the cache, `--strict` fails; a hung Graphviz is not asked for an SVG next; `0` runs nothing; `-1` lets a slow tool finish). Not tested on Windows: the runner uses `taskkill /T` and `shutil.which` for `mmdc.cmd`; the end-to-end tests there use shell-script stand-ins and are skipped, as the others in that file.
- README: "Diagram time limit" beside the LibreOffice one, and a sentence in the diagrams section. The `--help` text has no new flag.

## v3.32.0 — 2026-11-02

Pre-edit state: commit `394e482`. Opens the `\md{}` feature line, entry 3dc (queued 2026-10-26; the author, 2026-11-02: "i guess it is a good time to create that \md{} feature we were thinking of").

Markdown inside raw LaTeX. Raw LaTeX in a Markdown file reaches LaTeX untouched, so `*emphasis*`, `$x^2$` or `[@key]` inside a `\textbf{...}`, a `\caption{...}` or a hand-written `tabular` stayed as typed.

- `\md{...}` (one line or several) and `\begin{md}...\end{md}` hold Markdown: new `pdfmd_lua/md_macro.lua` splits the raw TeX Pandoc hands over into [raw TeX, the argument read as Markdown, raw TeX] with `pandoc.read`. It is the first of pdfmd's Lua filters, before pandoc-crossref and `--citeproc`, so a citation, an `@fig:x` reference, math or a footnote in the argument belongs to the one document.
- Where: a raw inline (`\textbf{\md{x}}`, a paragraph, heading, list item, table cell, caption) for every writer; a raw block such as a whole `tabular` or `figure` as one Plain block for LaTeX, Beamer and ConTeXt (the other writers drop that raw block as before); `\begin{md}` as real blocks (paragraphs, lists, tables) for every writer, also inside another raw environment. Several paragraphs in an inline `\md{}` are joined with a line break.
- The argument's braces must balance; a backslash escapes the next character (`\{`, `\}`), `%` and `#` are Markdown, not a TeX comment or parameter. A `\md` followed by a letter (`\mdseries`) is another command. An unbalanced `\md{` is read by Pandoc as plain text; the filter says so once with a WARN. `\begin{md}` has no brace counting, which is the way to write a code span with a lone brace.
- `md-macro: on` (the default) | `off` in `pdfmd-options`, with a `--setup` row (Input). The filter is loaded only for a document that has a macro outside code; a document that defines `\md` itself (`\newcommand`, `\def`, `\newenvironment{md}`) keeps its own and gets one NOTE.
- `contains_citations()` asks Pandoc with the filter on, so `--citeproc` is added for a document whose only citations are inside `\md{}`. A file with no front matter that uses the macro is read with Pandoc's `markdown` reader, not `gfm` (no raw LaTeX there), with the usual notice.
- Not done: the native (no-Pandoc) tier, a `.tex` source compiled directly, and the identity `.sty` for `~/dev/tex` (so the same `.tex` compiles without pdfmd), which is a step in the other repository.
- `tests/test_md_macro.py` (14 tests: detection outside code and own definitions, a macro inside `\textbf`, in a heading / bare line / list / table cell, in a raw `tabular` for LaTeX and HTML, the environment for tex / html / typst / md and inside `center`, citations resolved and listed, no front matter, `off`, a bad word, an own definition, an unbalanced brace, `\mdseries`). README: "Markdown inside raw LaTeX".

- Box-drawing tables (`┌─┬─┐ │ ├─┼─┤ └─┴─┘`, double, rounded and heavy): cells split on `│ ┃ ║`, a `|` inside a cell escaped; the first rule that contains `═` or `━` and is not the first or last is the header rule.
- psql output: the header line (no outer bars) above `----+----`, rows with as many bars, the `(N rows)` line dropped with the table.
- MySQL console output: a real grid table, no `=` rule, exactly three rules, a one-line header and two or more body lines, which Pandoc read as one joined row; each line is a row now. A body line with an empty first cell leaves the table alone, so a real grid table with a wrapped row is not touched; any other real grid table is never touched.
- The WARN names the form (`a box-drawing table was read as a pipe table (2 columns, 2 rows)`); the `--setup` row and the README section ("Text tables Pandoc cannot read") list the four spellings. Not done: the native tier, `<br>` in cells, org `|---+---|` and a pipe table without a separator row (queue items).
- Tests: `tests/test_table_ascii.py` (`Forms`, and a build for each of box, psql and lazy).

## v3.31.47 — 2026-11-02

Pre-edit state: commit `4761d60`. Still under 3.31. `[tables]`, entry 3el (the author pasted a table that NotebookLM wrote; "just implement it now under 3.31").

An ASCII table with no `+` at its column boundaries is read as a pipe table.

- Chat models write a "plain-text table" with `+-----+` borders that have no inner `+`, no `+===+` under the header, and `|` bars that drift by a character. Pandoc read it as one column without a header (every line a cell, the text off the page), and `table_width.lua` had nothing to balance. `pdfmd_tables/ascii.py` (new) repairs it before Pandoc sees it: a row is split on `|` (the bars' positions are not trusted), the lines between two borders are one row (wrapped cell lines joined with a space), the first row is the header (every row above a `+===+` line, if there is one), and the result is a pipe table with equal columns, which pdfmd's own width filter balances as it does any other. Rows with another number of cells than the header are padded or cut, each with a WARN.
- A real grid table (an inner `+`), a grid table of one column (no line with two cells), and anything inside a fenced or indented code block, an HTML comment or the YAML front matter are left alone. A literal `|` in a cell must be written `\|`.
- The text is changed in memory: `prepared_title_source()` (the document and a section built alone) and `scaffold_inputs()` (every part; the new `transform` argument) hand Pandoc a temporary copy, the file is never touched. One `WARN  table-ascii: FILE, line N: ...` for each table. Not done: the native (no-Pandoc) tier.
- `pdfmd-options: table-ascii: repair` (the default) | `note` (leave it, say so once for each table) | `off`; a `--setup` row (`pdfmd_setup/registry.py`) and its inventory entry. A word that is none of them stops the build. No number is a threshold.
- README: "A plain-text table from a chat model". Tests: `tests/test_table_ascii.py` (the function, then real builds: the default, `note`, `off`, a bad word, a real grid table, a part).

## v3.31.46 — 2026-11-02

Pre-edit state: commit `2a63449`. Still under 3.31 [tables]. Entry 3dy (the author's wish, 2026-10-31, with the answers of 2026-11-01/02).

A caption typed by hand next to a table can be the table's caption.

- `pdfmd_lua/table_caption.lua` (new, a Pandoc filter, so gfm and Pandoc Markdown alike): a paragraph that is entirely one bold span starting with a label word (`**Table 1: Results**`), right above a table without a caption (or else right below one; above wins), becomes its caption. The label and number are cut off (the engine numbers the table), the rest keeps its markup, a trailing `{#tbl:id}` becomes the table's id when it has none. A paragraph or heading between them, a bold line that is not alone in its paragraph, or a table that already has a caption: left alone. The number of blank lines does not matter.
- The label words come from `pdfmd_tables/captions.py` (English always, then the document's `lang:`: de, fr, es, it, pt, nl, pl, cs, sv, da, no, fi, ro, hu, el, bg, ru, uk, kk, tr, ar, zh, ja, ko), then `table-caption-words`: data, not code.
- Four `pdfmd-options` keys, each a `--setup` row (config and folder levels) and in the inventory: `table-captions` (`note`, the default: change nothing and say once, `NOTE  table-captions: N lines next to a table read like captions`; `on`; `off`), `table-caption-label` (`strip`, `keep`), `table-caption-need-label` (`on`; `off` takes any line that is one bold span, the author's "skip the label word" toggle) and `table-caption-colon-words` (0 = off, the author's "<= 2 words" sketch as a number: a gfm `: Results` of at most that many words is a caption too; Pandoc Markdown reads it by itself).
- The filter is added to the Pandoc command only for a document with a line that could be a caption, and after the CSV, markup and page-break filters.
- Tests: `tests/test_table_captions.py`.

## v3.31.44 — 2026-11-01

Pre-edit state: commit `c16091d`. Still under 3.31. Entry 3ef (the author's decision, with an example: the numbers of a part built alone are the numbers of the full build, names printing in the order they appear).

A part built alone sees the calculator's names of the whole document, below it as well as above it.

- Until now only the parts above the one built were evaluated (3.30.19), so a name defined in a later part was undefined in a part built alone, and the author had to build the Calculations part along with every part that prints its numbers. Now pdfmd reads the whole document with `calc.lua` alone (nothing typeset, about a second): the scaffold, then every part in order, a one-word paragraph `pdfmd-calc-mark-in` / `-out` around each part built. `calc.lua` writes (`-M pdfmd-calc-halves=FILE`) each name's last definition above the part built and its first definition below it, each evaluated in its own place, and the build reads them back, the first as before (`pdfmd-calc-seed`, standing above everything), the second as `pdfmd-calc-below` (standing after everything, so a name is taken from there only when nothing above or inside the part defines it). That is the full build's rule: the nearest definition above, else the first one below. With `x = 2` in the introduction, `y = x * 2` and then `x = 3` in the calculations, the procedure alone prints 2 and 4, the discussion alone 3 and 4, like the full build; the introduction alone, with every name below, works too.

The NOTE says where the names came from: `NOTE  calc: 128 names taken from parts 10-50, 3 from parts 70-90 (defined below) (evaluated, not typeset)`. The same `seed-calc` setting (`auto`, `scan`, `off`) governs both halves; no new setting. The export file (`calc: {export:}`) of a part built alone still lists the names above it and inside it only.
- KNOWN BUG, not fixed here (queued, entry 3eg): two parts built together that are not next to each other (`report#20+40`) take what the parts between them define as defined above both, so a number in part 20 can be the value a name gets only in part 30, silently. It was so before this version (the parts between were already read as "above"). Adjacent parts and sections are exact.

## v3.31.42 — 2026-10-31

Pre-edit state: commit `a609345`. Still under 3.31 (no minor before the tables are done). Entry 3ec (the author's wish: Obsidian draws SMILES through a plugin, pdfmd should draw the same notes). First slice of the `[smiles]` line.

A chemical structure written as text is drawn as a picture.

- `smiles` blocks, in the three spellings: a fenced ```` ```smiles ````, a fence with attributes ```` ```{.smiles caption="..." #fig:id} ````, and a `::: smiles` div (what Obsidian's chemistry plugins read, and what the calc blocks accept). A block is one structure per line, side by side (`per-row` to a row) under one caption; a name after the SMILES (`CCO ethanol`, the `.smi` convention) is written under that structure. `kind=` (`smiles`, `mol`, `mol2`, `inchi`, else read from the text or the file) and `file="x.mol"` (a file beside the document: `.mol`, `.sdf`, `.mol2`, `.smi`) are attributes of the block.
- The div form reads the body back as it was typed: Pandoc takes the nitro group `[N+](=O)[O-]` for a link, and the filter puts the link back together (`pdfmd_lua/smiles.lua`).
- Drawn by RDKit through `pdfmd_smiles`, one call of `python3 pdfmd_smiles` per document with pdfmd's own interpreter (RDKit is imported once; nothing is shelled to another Python). Every structure has the same bond length (`bond-length`), so a small molecule is not drawn large. Format by output: PDF for LaTeX (through `rsvg-convert`; PNG when there is none), SVG for HTML, EPUB and Typst, PNG for Word and OpenDocument (`office-format: svg` for SVG; Word 365 and LibreOffice read it, older Word, Google Docs and Pages do not), an SVG beside the output for flat Markdown (`--to gfm`, as diagrams are). A captioned block is a figure; `{#fig:id}` reaches pandoc-crossref.
- The picture cache is keyed by everything that changes the picture: the engine and its version, the kind, the structures, the format, the cell size, the columns, the bond length, the dpi and the module's own version. The same block twice is drawn once; the same block with another engine, format or setting is a new picture, never a stale one. (The chemfig engine's compiled cache, `cache: {smiles}`, comes with that engine.)
- A block that cannot be drawn (RDKit missing, a structure that does not read, a missing file, an unknown setting in the block) stays as code with one warning that says why; a wrong `pdfmd-options.smiles` stops the build and names the key.
- Settings, all under one key, `pdfmd-options.smiles`, and every one also an attribute of a block (`columns=` for `per-row`): `engine` (`auto`, `rdkit`), `format` (`auto`, `svg`, `png`, `pdf`), `office-format` (`png`, `svg`), `cell-width` (250), `cell-height` (200), `per-row` (3), `bond-length` (40), `dpi` (300). The numbers are the author's to change, not constants: each is a `--setup` row (Chemical structures) and a folder setting.
- `--no-auto smiles` leaves the blocks as code. `--doctor` says whether RDKit is installed.
- A Markdown file with no front matter is read as gfm, which has neither the div nor code attributes: the note about what gfm leaves as plain text now also names a fence that opens with attributes (```` ```{.smiles caption=... } ````, ```` ```{.d2 ...} ````), as it names `:::` divs.
- `CLAUDE.md` names the new `[smiles]` tag next to `[kits]` and `[tables]`.
- `scripts/build_zipapp.py` lists `pdfmd_smiles` and, which it was missing since the kits line, `pdfmd_kits` (`tests/test_packaging.py` compares it with the wheel's list and was failing).
- Tests: `tests/test_smiles.py` (settings, reading, drawing and the cache, no RDKit, builds through `pdfmd` itself).

## v3.31.41 — 2026-10-31

Pre-edit state: commit `437c3ef`. Still under 3.31 (no minor before the tables are done). Entry 3ea (the author's wish, from a `FOUND` line that printed the long path of a course folder's `.pdfmd/`).

A path in a message is written as short as it can be, by a setting.

- Cause: `display_path` wrote a path relative to the working folder only when it was under it, so a folder above it (a course folder's `.pdfmd/`, a shared metadata file) fell back to the absolute path.
- `path-style` (`auto`, `relative`, `home`, `full`; `--path-style`, `options.path-style`, a `--setup` row under Messages). `auto` (the default): relative to the working folder, up to `path-up` `..` steps above it (`--path-up N`, `options.path-up`, a `--setup` row, default 2: the author's number, a setting and not a constant), else `~/...` under the home folder (the same on every system, `~\` separators on Windows), else absolute. `relative` is that without `~`, `home` is `~/...` whenever the file is under the home folder, `full` is `--full-paths`.
- Both settings work at every level: the command line, the config file (`--setup`) and a folder's own settings (`pdfmd --setup DIR`, `.pdfmd/config.yaml`; the nearest folder wins, read at the first document of the run, as the style is one for the whole run). They are not `pdfmd-options` keys of a document.
- `--verbose` and `--debug` still write full paths, as before (the author asked to keep that); an explicit `--path-style` on the same command line wins. Only what is printed changes; the manifests, the caches and the commands' own arguments keep real paths.
- A symlink is still written where it sits, as before.
- The `CMD` line (`--verbose`, and the build record) is a command to run again, so it never uses `..`: a path under the working folder is relative, under the home folder `~/...` (outside the quotes, so a shell expands it), else absolute; `full` (so also `--verbose`) keeps every path absolute. The copy of the line in the build record, written whatever `--verbose` said, follows the style, so the account name stays out of it.
- Setup: the two rows are in a folder's setup too (`FOLDER_OPTIONS`); the inventory has `--path-style`, `--path-up` and the keys.
- Tests: `tests/test_path_display.py`.

## v3.31.40 — 2026-10-31

Pre-edit state: commit `25ec92a`. Still under 3.31. `[kits]`, entry 3du, point 20 (the author's wish: a course whose lab partners rotate).

A metadata value can add to the layers below instead of replacing them.

- `author+: [B]` in any layer is the value the layers below hold, then `B` (a single value is a list of one; nothing below, just `B`); `author:` and `author+:` in one place are taken in that order. `pdfmd-options.metadata-append: [author]` (a name or a list; `--setup` row *Keys whose document value adds to the layers below*, folders may set it) makes the document's own value add too.
- The layers, lowest first, are the global metadata, a kit's defaults, the folders' `.pdfmd/metadata.yaml` (the farthest first), the document folder's metadata files and the document's front matter; `tests/test_metadata_append.py` pins that order, which was already how a build behaved.
- Pandoc cannot do it (the document's front matter beats every metadata file), so pdfmd merges the layers and hands the finished values over in a metadata file under `pdfmd-merged`; `pdfmd_lua/metadata_append.lua` runs before every other filter, sets them and removes the `key+` keys. A build with no plus key and no setting adds no argument at all.
- A mapping cannot be added to and `header-includes` is not supported (pdfmd lifts it into header files itself): both stop with a message naming the file.
- An assembled or attached source holds the finished value and no `key+`, and its `pdfmd-options` says `metadata-append: []` (the same reason as `kit: none`, 3.31.38): a restored report rebuilds elsewhere with each name once.
- Not covered: the built-in renderer (no Pandoc) does not run Lua filters, so it takes the layers as before and does not add.
- Setup: the `options.metadata-append` row, and the key in `pdfmd_setup/inventory.py`.
- Tests: `tests/test_metadata_append.py` (11: the order, `+` in each layer, both keys in one place, the setting in the config and in the document, markup in a name, a mapping and `header-includes`, the source and a rebuild in another folder).

## v3.31.39 — 2026-10-31

Pre-edit state: commit `6120d64`. Still under 3.31. `[tables]`, entry 3dz (reported by the author from a pK table).

CSV rows typed straight into a `::: {.csv}` block keep their inline markup.

- Cause: Pandoc has parsed the lines of such a block as a paragraph before the filter sees them; `pdfmd_lua/csv_table.lua` rebuilt the text from the paragraph's inlines and flattened every one but words, quotes and code with `stringify`, so `p*K*~1~` reached the cell reader as `pK1`. A `file=` block and a fenced body never went through that, and neither did a pipe table; `\ce{..}` and `$..$` survived only because Pandoc keeps them as plain text.

Where that write fails the old flattening is the fallback.
- Tests: `tests/test_csv_table.py` (`InlineData`): the markup reaches the cells, and the straight form and the fenced form of one table give the same document. Both fail without the change.

## v3.31.35 — 2026-10-31

Pre-edit state: commit `6ab64f0`. Still under 3.31. `[kits]`, C4 of entry 3du (the kit's part).

An attached or assembled source holds what a chosen kit wrote and the kit's parts, so a restored report rebuilds on a machine with no kit.

- **The preamble.** `--attach-source`, `--keep-source`, `--bundle` and `--embed-metadata` put the kit's header (`\usepackage[<options>]{package}`, its `latex:` lines) first among the embedded preambles, and the found preambles as the build read them: what the kit writes twice is settled in them (`KIT-SAME`, `KIT-MERGE`, `KIT-YIELD`), so a rebuild gets the same LaTeX in the same order and `Option clash` cannot come back. The settling is one function for the build and the source (`kit_header_settle`).
- **The parts.** The files a kit's `carry:` names are stored beside the document whether or not the folder is bundled: a named file keeps its path, a named folder is carried by its files (flat), a name the document's folder holds is left to the folder, a name that is not in the kit is a NOTE, a kit over `bundle-max-mb` is not carried (WARN). They go in before the bundle's own TeX-tree files, so the kit's copy wins. The manifest gets `kits: [{name, version, mode, package, carried}]` (additive; `ATTACH_FORMAT` stays 2); `--restore` prints a `KIT` line and labels the files "from a kit".
- Checked on a copy of a real report with real lualatex: the report built with `kit: nulabreport:qca` and a course `.pdfmd/`, attached, restored, and rebuilt in the restored folder with no config, no kit and an empty `TEXMFHOME`, is pixel-identical.

## v3.31.32 — 2026-10-31

Pre-edit state: commit `1ee4fb9`. Still under 3.31. `[kits]`, C3 of entry 3du.

A chosen kit writes its own preamble, and what it and the user's LaTeX say twice is settled in the build copy (3du, point 9).

- **The kit's lines come first.** One header file, `\usepackage[<mode options>]{package}`, then the kit's `latex:` lines and its mode's, goes ahead of every other `--include-in-header` (after pdfmd's code-wrapping header), so `\labsetup{...}` and the like in `preamble.tex`, `header-includes:` (the document's or a folder's metadata) or an `--include-in-header` file follow it. A kit's `latex-keys` now apply with no `preamble.tex` of the user's.
- **Four outcomes** for the user's text, in copies in the cache folder (a user's file is never edited): the same line (the package with options the kit already gives, or an `\input` the kit writes) is dropped, `KIT-SAME`; extra options (`[qca,draft]` against `[qca]`) are merged into the kit's one line, `KIT-MERGE` (LaTeX itself stops on two different `\usepackage` lines of one package: "Option clash"); an option that belongs to another mode of the same kit is a contradiction: a preamble found in the folder yields with a WARN, `KIT-YIELD`, its line commented out, while `header-includes:`, an `--include-in-header` file or a named `preamble:` stop the build naming both sides; everything else stays after the kit's lines with no word. `KIT-SAME` and `KIT-MERGE` show with `--verbose`; the ids are fixed for the chatter ladder to come.
- Only a whole-line `\usepackage[...]{name}` (options may span lines; `\RequirePackage` too) and a whole-line `\input{...}` are rewritten. The kit's package behind a macro or inside a list (`\usepackage{a,labstyle}`) stops the build and names the line; an `\input` in another shape is left alone.
- `keep_header_includes` (the one place the finished command's header files are settled) does the work for every route; `document_header_file` is active when a kit writes a preamble, so the document's own `header-includes` are not dropped. Pure part: `pdfmd_kits/preamble.py`; tests: `tests/test_kit_preamble.py` (the resolver as a table, builds through pdfmd, and a real `pdflatex` run that survives the user's added option).

## v3.31.31 — 2026-10-31

Pre-edit state: commit `abe26bb`. Still under 3.31. `[kits]`, C2 of entry 3du.

A document can choose a kit, and the kit's defaults, Lua filters and folder reach the build. (The preamble a kit writes is the next patch; until then a kit's package is loaded by the document's own preamble.)

- **Choosing.** `pdfmd-options: {kit: ...}` in a document, a metadata file, a folder's `.pdfmd/` files, a preset or the config's `options:`; `--kit` on the command line. The value reads `nulabreport`, `nulabreport:qca` (no quotes needed), `nulabreport[qca]`, `"[qca]nulabreport"` (quoted), `{nulabreport: qca}`, `{nulabreport: {mode: qca}}`, a list for the order, a path (a value with `/`, `\` or a leading `~` or `.`), and `none|off|false|no` for no kit. A mode is matched by name or alias, ignoring case and `- _ .` and spaces; an unknown mode stops and lists the modes. README, section "Kits".
- **Layers stack**, lowest first: the config's `kit:` (global), the global metadata or a preset, the folders' files (farthest first), the document's metadata files and front matter. The same kit named higher up replaces only the keys it names (a mode, say); different kits are added in order; `none` drops what is below. A folder's `kit:` names a kit and never searches the project's `kits/` folder or takes a path (a folder's options cannot name code); a message says so.
- **`--kit`** replaces every `kit:` setting; repeated `--kit` stacks in order; `--kit none`, or a bare `--kit` before another option, means no kit. **`--kit-stack`** (also `pdfmd-options: {kit-stack: ...}` and a `--setup` row) says what `--kit` stacks on instead of replacing: `off` (default), `all`, or a list of `global`, `preset`, `folder`, `document`. Switches stay absolute whatever it says. `kit` and `kit-stack` are `--setup` rows ("Kits").
- **What a chosen kit brings.** Its `defaults:` files, its inline `metadata:`, its mode's `defaults:` and `metadata:` as metadata files between the global metadata and the folders' own (the folder tunes the kit; the document wins; inline metadata is written once into `kit-metadata/` of the cache folder, named by its content); its `lua:` filters; its folder on Pandoc's resource path, so its `csl:` and `bibliography:` are found by name; its package, so `package_helper` and the Lua and Word lookups see it, and `kit_package_folders` (the 3.31.29 slot) answers; the helper blocks of its `.kit` (`latex-keys`, `draft-skip`, `office`, `lua`...) when no `<package>-pdfmd.yaml` stands beside the `.sty`. `--verbose` prints an `AUTO KIT` line per chosen kit. A document that no layer gives a `kit:` is read as before; the kit code is not imported.
- Tests: `tests/test_kit_selection.py` (the grammar as a table, YAML spellings, stacking, `--kit` and `kit-stack`, and builds through pdfmd itself with a fixture kit).

README, section "Kits".

- `--no-auto kit` takes the searching off (a registered `kits:` folder and a path stay); `--no-auto kpsewhich` only the TeX tree.
- `pdfmd --kits` lists the kits and their modes; `pdfmd --kits NAME-OR-PATH` shows one in full and checks it, with "did you mean" for a near name. `kits:` is a config key (a `--setup` row, *Folders of kits*, this computer only); `--kits` is an `Omitted` command in the inventory; tests: `tests/test_kits.py`.

## v3.31.29 — 2026-10-31

Pre-edit state: commit `c268035`. Still under 3.31.

A lone copy of a package's `.sty` beside the document no longer loses what the package tells pdfmd about itself (3dw).

- Cause: TeX takes `<package>.sty` beside the document first, and pdfmd read `<package>-pdfmd.yaml` only in the folder of the `.sty` it had taken. A report folder holding just `nulabreport.sty` therefore had no `latex-keys:`: the experiment number printed `N/A`, and the performance date and the unknowns line were gone, with no message. (The same gap hid `lua:`, `office:` and `draft-skip:`.) The hard-coded table of those keys was removed in 3.28.37 on purpose ("pdfmd names no package") and stays removed.
- `package_helper` now looks for the file in this order: beside the `.sty` the document uses (as before), beside the `.sty` of a selected kit that ships the package (kits are not built yet: the place is asked and answers nothing), then beside the installed copy `kpsewhich` finds (asked from an empty folder: TeX searches the current folder first, so from the document's own it answers with the lone copy). The file found keeps its own path, so the names it lists resolve beside it. A helper beside the lone copy still wins. The last two places are searched only when the first has none, so a build whose package carries its file pays nothing.
- Two `--no-auto` kinds, `kit` and `kpsewhich` (`pdfmd-options: {no-auto: [kpsewhich]}` too, and a `--setup` row each), take one place off; a bare `--no-auto` takes both. On by default: a copy older than the installed helper fails loudly (a `\renewcommand` of a macro it lacks), where without the fallback it printed `N/A` silently.
- `no_auto` now reaches `package_latex_keys`, `package_lua_names`, `find_lua_filters`, `package_draft_skips`, `document_header_file` and `office_defaults_sources`.
- Checked through pdfmd itself: a copy of a real 28-page report with a lone `nulabreport.sty` beside it printed `#N/A` for the experiment before, and builds with the same text on every page as the copy without one now.
- Tests (`tests/test_package_helper.py`): the lone copy reads the installed helper for keys, Lua names and draft skips; the helper beside it wins; `kpsewhich` and a bare `--no-auto` stop the borrowing and `kit` does not; a kit's folder is asked before the installed copy.

## v3.31.20 — 2026-10-31

Pre-edit state: commit `db904bd`. Still under 3.31.

`pdfmd --crop FILE.pdf...` cuts a finished PDF to what it draws. It is the crop of eqpop (the macOS popup that renders a formula to a cropped PDF), made portable so eqpop can later hand the job to pdfmd.

- The ink of each page is what Ghostscript's `bbox` device finds painted (the same measurement `pdfmd_office/fragments.py` uses for a fragment); pypdf then sets the media box and the crop box (and the trim, bleed and art boxes if the page has them) to that box plus a pad, never beyond the page's own box. The page stays vector. A rotated page is measured as displayed and cut in its own coordinates; a page that draws nothing is left as it is, with a NOTE.
- The result is `NAME-crop.pdf` beside the source (the source is never changed), `-o FILE` for one PDF or `-o FOLDER` for several; `-o` the source itself crops in place, through a `.part` file.
- Settings, each a flag with its default written in `--help`: `--crop-pad PT` (default 2), `--crop-ignore-bottom PT` (default 0; leaves the foot of each page out of the measurement, e.g. a page number), `--crop-page N` (keep that page alone; default every page, each to its own ink). They are `--setup`-omitted (about one run), like `--check-docx`.
- New package `pdfmd_crop` (`crop_pdf`, `ink_boxes`); `--help crop` is its topic. Without Ghostscript or pypdf the command says what to install.
- Test: `tests/test_crop.py` (pages drawn by Ghostscript from PostScript, so the ink is known: pad, foot, one page, rotation by 90/180/270, a blank page, in place, the command line).

## v3.31.19 — 2026-10-30

Pre-edit state: commit `aeaad80`. Still under 3.31. Merged from a pull request of the Windows test session.

The plot cache records the files a plot job read, and drops any that is not under the report's folders. TeX writes a Windows drive letter in lower case (`d:/work/lab/ir/product.csv`) where the report's folder is `D:\work\lab`, and the comparison was case-sensitive, so every CSV was dropped as foreign and an edit to it showed as a stale plot. `plot_recorded_inputs` now compares through `os.path.normcase` on both sides (the identity on macOS and Linux).

- Found by the nulabreport smoke test on Windows: after a CSV edit the cached build differed from the uncached one in 96 of 1114 words; with the fix the checks pass and the `.deps` files list the CSVs.
- Test: `tests/test_plot_cache.py` (`test_a_lower_case_drive_letter_is_still_the_reports_folder`), Windows only, fails without the fix.

- **`pdfmd --user-path add|remove|show [FOLDER...]` (Windows): put folders on the user PATH, and take them off again.** Spelled-out forms: `--add-to-path`, `--remove-from-path`, `--show-user-path`; `--yes` skips the question, `--dry-run` writes nothing. Opt-in only: nothing in pdfmd calls it by itself. It writes `Path` under `HKEY_CURRENT_USER\Environment` (no administrator rights), keeps the registry type (`setx` would cut the value at 1024 characters and turn it into `REG_SZ`), copies every other entry byte for byte and appends at the end so a new folder never shadows a program of the machine PATH. `add` with no folder takes the folders of the tools pdfmd found off PATH (3.31.10); a folder you name may be any existing folder. It lists what it will do and asks first (no terminal or `PDFMD_NO_PROMPT` without `--yes` refuses); folders already on the user or machine PATH are skipped; the running programs are told (`WM_SETTINGCHANGE`) and the PowerShell line that refreshes the current window is printed. What was added is recorded in `path-added.json` in pdfmd's settings folder (state, not a setting); `remove` takes off exactly those entries and leaves a folder the user already removed alone. On macOS and Linux the command exits 1 and prints the `export PATH=...` line for the shell profile.
- **A new kind of `--setup` row: an action** (`pdfmd_setup/__init__.py` takes `actions=`; the plain and the full-screen setup both draw it). The first is "Windows user PATH" in "Tool locations" (add the found folders / add a folder you name / show / undo); per machine, shown on Windows only, never in a folder's setup.
- `--doctor` ends with one note on Windows when tools it found are not on the user PATH.
- The code is `pdfmd_setup/userpath.py` (four-method backend: `Registry` is the real one, tests use a fake and, on Windows, a throwaway key named by `PDFMD_USER_ENV_KEY`, a test-only variable); `tests/test_user_path.py` (26 tests). Decision 3dr of the maintainer's notes; by the Windows test session (pull request #35).

## v3.31.16 — 2026-10-31

Pre-edit state: commit `e9445e7`. Still under 3.31. Merged from a pull request of the Windows test session.

### Added
- **`soffice-timeout`: a LibreOffice run has a time limit.** Every start of LibreOffice (the Office converter and the `-e soffice` route, the ODF reader of hybrid builds, spreadsheets read through it, the SVG converter) goes through one runner, `run_soffice()`: a run that takes longer than the limit is stopped together with the processes it started (the process group on macOS and Linux, `taskkill /T` on Windows), and its file fails with a message that names the setting; the other files of a batch go on. Default 300 seconds. **`0`: LibreOffice is never run** (it counts as not installed; `--doctor` says it is turned off). **A negative number (`-1`): no limit.** The key is in `pdfmd-options` (per document, and in a folder's setup), the config and `pdfmd --setup` ("Checks and limits"); no command-line flag. The two hard-coded limits it replaces (120 s for an SVG, 180 s for a sheet) are gone; the packages take the runner as an argument (`run=`), and without one keep their old limit. `tests/test_soffice_timeout.py`. Decision 3ds of the maintainer's notes.

### Notes
- The default is a constant the author has not confirmed as a number (300); a first start with a new profile takes 20 to 30 seconds and a large document more, so a low default would break working builds.

## v3.31.5 — 2026-10-29

Pre-edit state: commit `3cb13f4`. Still under 3.31, in front of the rest of the tables work.

### Added
- **The record of a build.** Every build writes a plain-text file to the cache: the command line, the versions (pdfmd, Python, Pandoc, the engines), every
  command run (the `CMD` lines, whatever `--verbose` said), everything pdfmd printed, what each engine answered (exit code, stderr, stdout), the steps and their
  times, and what the build answered; the home folder is written as `~`. It sits where `cache: location` says (`~/.cache/pdfmd/builds/NAME-HASH/`, or
  `.cache/pdfmd/builds/NAME/` beside the document), one file per build (`20261029-140533-ok.log`, `-failed.log`). A failed build ends with `full record: PATH`
  (`--verbose` also names the record of a good one); a build that stopped with an error is recorded too.
- **`pdfmd --last-build FILE [--failed]`** prints the newest record, or the newest failed one; none: a message and exit status 1.
- **`build-log: on|failed|off`** (default on; `--build-log MODE`), **`build-log-keep`** (default 5; the newest ones stay, and the newest failed one whatever its age,
  so a good build never erases a failure) and **`build-log-max-size`** (KB, default 512; a longer record keeps its start and more of its end), in `pdfmd-options`,
  the config and `--setup`.
- The package `pdfmd_buildinfo.record` (pure): scrubbing, clipping, naming, atomic writing and pruning.

### Notes
- A first version, built from the central points (no `emit` yet): the lines that only `--verbose` prints at their own print sites are not in the record until every
  message goes through one function. A `.qmd`, a direct `.typ`/`.html` build and a report or book build are not recorded yet. A record that cannot be written
  (read-only or full disk) never fails a build.
- `tests/test_00_environment.py` turns the record off for the suite as a whole (it would make a record for each of the thousand documents the tests build); the
  tests of the record ask for it.

## v3.31.4 — 2026-10-29

### Added
- **How long a build took.** The closing line ends in the time, `OK    report.md > report.pdf  in 3:07  (lualatex)`, also for a file that failed
  (`FAIL  report.md  in 0.15 s`) and for a report or book build. Written by `time-format` (the new package `pdfmd_buildinfo`): `auto` (the default;
  `0.42 s`, `12.4 s`, `3:07`, `1:02:03`, `1 d 02:03:04`), `clock` (`03:07`; hours never wrap into days), `seconds`, `words`, or a template with
  `{d} {h} {hh} {m} {mm} {s} {ss} {s1} {s2} {ms}`; a unit wraps only under a larger one of the template, and the time is rounded to the smallest unit shown.
- **`build-time: on|off`** (default on) and **`time-format`**, in `pdfmd-options`, the config, `--setup`, and as `--build-time` / `--no-build-time` and
  `--time-format STYLE`. A wrong format stops the command line and warns for a document (it reads as `auto`).
- **`--verbose` prints a `TIME` line for every step**: the engine run (`pandoc + lualatex`; a font retry is a second line), the label and calc passes, plots,
  polish, attach-source, backup, history, the size budget; and "the rest" (finding files and settings, the pre-passes no step covers).

Pre-edit state: commit `4d6291b`. Still the tables line: the settings of the width filter are named for what they set, and none of their numbers is a constant.

  settings; they were constants in the filter. Every number of the filter (`column-outlier` too) can be given per table, `{column-outlier=3
